files.contentPreview: [[Ampure_Data::Cross-Vault Resolver Target]] Cross-Vault Link Test Goal Verify that `Test_Vault_` can reference content owned by `Ampure_Data` without copying that content. Resolver test The lightweight resolver plugin is the current MVP. 1. Make sure `Test_Vault_` and `Ampure_Data` are sibling folders on the same computer. 2. Pull both repositories. 3. Reload Obsidian. 4. In this note, type: ```text [[Cross-Vault Resolver Target ``` 5. Choose the result labeled from **Ampure Data**. 6. The inserted link should be UID-backed and readable. 7. Click it. Expected target: ```text Cross-Vault Resolver Target ``` Expected behavior: Obsidian opens the target note in `Ampure_Data`. Canonical durable format Stored cross-vault references use: ```text [Readable title](uid:<30-character-note-uid>) ``` Optional section target: ```text [Readable section](uid:<30-character-note-uid>#<section-anchor>) ``` The note UID is durable. Vault name and path are only current location metadata. View-level rule

files.contentPreview: Organizational Vault Standard This note captures the approved organization-wide vault structure and usability rules developed after the initial shared-vault baseline. It defines the target reusable starter behavior. It does **not** by itself authorize a destructive migration of the current `Ampure_Data` folder tree. Design Principle Keep vaults stable, understandable, and usable during normal work. Prefer simple human workflows over continuous background restructuring. Structural cleanup, consistency checks, and generated support-file updates are performed periodically through an AI-assisted maintenance pass. When a vault becomes too large for a high-quality review, reduce the maintenance scope rather than reducing review quality. File Naming All user-facing files use human-readable filenames based on the canonical name of the thing they represent. Examples: - `Ampure.md` - `Engineering.md` - `John Smith.md` - `Engineering Change.md` - `New Charger Platform.md` Do not use opaque IDs, G

files.contentPreview: Governance Rules Approved Content - `main` is the approved vault state. - Normal contributors do not write directly to `main`. - Human and AI changes enter through pull requests. - Either authorized approver may approve and merge. - Approvers have full authority, including on their own proposals. - Editing a proposal is not approval; approval remains an explicit action. Proposal Ownership - Human contributors use short-lived review branches. - AI contributors use isolated task branches. - A proposal may accumulate edits until its review batch is completed. - The author may edit any file on their own proposal branch. - Other normal users may view and comment, but not edit that branch. - Approvers may edit any proposal. - Do not rewrite contributor history with force pushes. Deferred Work - Unaccepted recommendations may remain open with a `deferred` label. - Deferred proposals remain visible and commentable. - They are retained until explicitly revised, accepted, withdrawn, or closed. -

files.contentPreview: Architecture System - **Obsidian** — normal human interface. - **GitHub** — authoritative store and approved history. - **Sync agent** — one machine-level process managing all locally authorized vaults. - **GitHub workflow** — proposals, review, validation, approval, and merge. - **AI tools** — contributors using the same proposal workflow as people. Normal users should not need to operate Git. Vault Model Use independent sibling repositories, not nested Git repositories. - **Shared vault** — common company knowledge, standards, instructions, and references. - **Scoped vaults** — role-, project-, function-, or access-limited work. - Shared information stays authoritative in one location and is referenced rather than copied. - Repository access determines whether a user can access a scoped vault. - The sync agent registers only vaults the authenticated user can access. The shared vault may help bootstrap or register the sync agent, but does not contain the agent executable. Local vs Git

Role A responsibility or participation position that may be filled by one or more people. Examples: - Design Engineer - Quality Manager - Project Manager - Approver - Supplier Representative Roles are appropriate participants in process definitions. Human review does not automatically mean approval. A definition can be reviewed while remaining `proposed`. files.contentPreview: Artifact Storage Defines the organization-wide storage pattern for non-Markdown source files. Shared Folder Use a common top-level artifact area: ```text 70_Artifacts/ Images/ Documents/ Spreadsheets/ Diagrams/ CAD/ Media/ Other/ ``` Rule Markdown notes and modeled elements carry the semantic context, provenance, relationships, and human-readable explanation. Native artifacts remain in `70_Artifacts` when their original format matters. Do not place artifacts beside notes merely for convenience if that makes them harder to find, reuse, migrate, or manage later. Reuse One artifact may support multiple notes or modeled elements. References should point to the artifact rather than duplicating the file into multiple folders. Fidelity Preserve original files when conversion would lose technical, evidentiary, visual, or legal value.

Enterprise Tool Integration Direction The vault should remain the durable knowledge layer while external business systems continue to own their operational data. Current integration targets - **Jira** — task and issue management remains in Jira. Vault content may reference Jira work, summarize it, or derive durable knowledge from it. - **Rovo** — may read and write approved vault content where permissions allow, and may use vault + Jira context to create or update derived knowledge. - **Confluence** — may receive published or synthesized pages generated from

files.contentPreview: Ordinary Note vs Modeled Element Defines when information should remain a normal Markdown note and when it should become a modeled MDSE element. Default Rule Use an **ordinary note** when the information is mainly for people to read. Use a **modeled element** when the information needs its own durable identity and should participate in structured relationships, validation, reuse, or automation. Do not model information merely because it can be modeled. Use an Ordinary Note When Typical examples include: - meeting notes - research - explanations - working thoughts - summaries - instructions - general documentation - temporary analysis - narrative context An ordinary note may still have a UID and may link to modeled elements. files.contentPreview: UID Assignment for Notes Defines when Markdown notes receive an organization UID. Default Rule Every Markdown note created by a user should receive a UID at creation. This applies even when the note begins as: - a scratch note - a temporary checklist - pasted working text - an experiment - an incomplete thought - a draft that may later be discarded The reason is simple: information that looks temporary when created may later become valuable, linked, reviewed, reused, or promoted into a modeled element. Exceptions A Markdown file may omit an assigned UID only when adding a persistent identity would interfere with its intended use. Examples may include: - generated files owned by another tool - imported source files that must remain byte-for-byte unchanged - machine-generated intermediate artifacts - files whose external format contract forbids added metadata - reusable note templates whose `uid:` field is intentionally blank so each created note receives a new identity Exceptions must b

files.contentPreview: Security and Access Roles Contributor - read approved content - create and update their own proposals - view and comment on all visible proposals - defer or withdraw their own proposals - cannot approve or merge into `main` Approver - all contributor capabilities - edit any proposal - approve and merge any proposal - resolve conflicts and administer proposal state - may approve and merge their own proposal AI Contributor - uses an isolated proposal branch - follows the same approval gate as a human contributor - has only the authority explicitly granted to its credential Enforcement Documentation is not a security boundary. Enforce important controls with GitHub permissions, rulesets/branch protection, required reviews, CODEOWNERS where useful, and scoped authentication. Do not rely on the local sync agent alone to prevent unauthorized branch changes. Audience Assume the reader has no background in Git, GitHub, terminals, shells, Obsidian internals, plugins, or software administration. files.contentPreview: Vault Architecture and Cross-Vault Rules Vault model Use independent sibling Git repositories, never nested repositories. `Ampure_Data` is the shared/common company vault. Scoped domain/product vaults own their domain-specific semantics. Users create vaults. AI may flag when scale, access, lifecycle, search, or AI-context quality suggests a split, but it does not autonomously create or split vaults. Stable identity Each vault has permanent `vault_uid` in root `.vault.yaml`. Each durable note has immutable `uid`. Canonical reference: ```text uid:<30-character-id> ``` Optional section reference: ```text uid:<30-character-id>#<section-anchor> ``` Paths and vault names are location metadata, not durable identity. Cross-vault links Note-to-note semantic relationships target the specific note UID. files.contentPreview: Cross-Vault Link Test Goal Verify that this new vault can reference content owned by another locally available vault without copying that content. Test 1 — current/native Obsidian behavior Until the UID resolver plugin is implemented, use an Obsidian URI as a **temporary transport test**: ```text [Open Ampure_Data README](obsidian://open?vault=Ampure_Data&file=README.md) ``` This proves that both vaults can be opened and addressed locally. It is **not** the durable production link format because vault names and paths can change. Test 2 — canonical durable format Production cross-vault references use: ```text [Readable title](uid:<30-character-note-uid>) ``` Optional section target: ```text [Readable section](uid:<30-character-note-uid>#<section-anchor>) ``` The future resolver plugin will translate the UID to the current accessible vault/path. files.contentPreview: MDSE Bootstrap Architecture Purpose Make a copied or cloned MDSE base vault operational without requiring the user to understand Git internals, Obsidian community-plugin installation, or MDSE support-file dependencies. Bootstrap is deliberately split into three layers. 1. Initialize `Initialize-Vault.sh` / `Initialize-Vault.ps1` One-time operation that: - assigns the immutable vault UID; - writes the vault display name; - preserves `main` as the default branch; - invokes provisioning. A populated `.vault.yaml` is never overwritten automatically. 2. Provision `Provision-Vault.sh` / `Provision-Vault.ps1` Machine-local operation that: - verifies prerequisites; - creates a local Git repository when one is absent; - sets `pull.ff=only`; - optionally configures `origin`; - installs the bundled MDSE Bootstrap plugin; - installs the exact third-party plugin versions pinned in `.obsidian/plugin-lock.yaml`. Third-party plugin repository locations are resolved from Obsidian's official community p

Identity Registry — source GUID ↔ MDSE ID/UID ↔ filepath/current vault. 2. Transformation Log — merges, collapses, semantic remaps, suppressions, renames. 3. Model Checks — ambiguity, naming, relationship, and source-model issues. 4. Pending Relationships — unresolved endpoints, including cross-package/cross-vault endpoints. Engineering migration direction 1. Import EA content into the engineering staging/base vault. 2. Classify and normalize semantics without inventing missing facts. 3. Establish stable note UIDs before splitting. 4. Split notes into Engineering Common and product-line vaults based on semantic ownership. 5. files.contentPreview: Git and New Vault Setup Purpose Create or recover a fully operational MDSE vault with Git and the required Obsidian feature stack. Prerequisites - Obsidian - Git - access to the target GitHub repository when using a remote - internet access during initial community-plugin provisioning - macOS/Linux: `curl` and `python3` GitHub Desktop is supported but optional. It does not replace the Git executable required by Obsidian Git. New vault procedure 1. Copy/unzip the reusable MDSE base into a new folder, or clone a repository intentionally created from it. 2. Run the platform initializer from the vault folder. 3. The initializer creates the unique `.vault.yaml` identity and invokes provisioning. 4. Provisioning creates a local Git repository if one does not already exist. 5. Provisioning sets `git config pull.ff only`. 6. If a remote URL is supplied, provisioning configures it as `origin`. 7. files.contentPreview: MDSE Modeling Ruleset 1.19 Status Current reusable modeling ruleset for new Ampure vaults. 1. Model meaning before structure Classify the concept semantically before choosing a type. Search for an existing authoritative definition before creating a new one. Prefer reuse, then instance, true specialization, decomposition, and only then a new independent concept. Folder placement is navigation only. 2. Generalization Use `subtypeOf` only for a reusable invariant semantic distinction. Use `instanceOf` for concrete occurrences, deployed/location-specific objects, configured realizations, or cases where the difference is ordinary data/configuration. 3. Product control `control` is independent from type and boundary. Do not create subtypes just to represent control, ownership, location, or lifecycle. 4. files.contentPreview: Vault Architecture and Cross-Vault Rules Repository model Use independent sibling Git repositories. Do not nest repositories. Each vault is independently permissioned and independently cloneable. Current organizational direction - `Ampure_Data` — common company vault. - Engineering import/staging vault — receives EA data before product-line separation. - Product-line engineering vaults — EVSE, GSE, MHE, BMID, EMS. - Engineering Common — shared engineering/product definitions that are genuinely cross-product. - Additional vaults are created only when authority, confidentiality, workflow, lifecycle, scale, search, or AI-context quality justifies the boundary. Authority Company/shared identities stay authoritative in `Ampure_Data`. Engineering technical definitions stay authoritative in the responsible engineering vault. files.contentPreview:
Individual Asset Registration (Vehicle) Allow users to register a single asset manually into the system. EA Note eaGUID: {C2A7634C-2EA4-40e2-8D3E-6A902D05636A} Break up "asset registration" into separate use cases - vehicle, accessory (skylink kit, stack light), charger, etc. EA Note eaGUID: {F0AFB81C-6F4A-4ce7-90AB-0969A9254015} System Notes: Data Validation:
  • Validate unique identifiers (Vehicle ID, BMID Serial Number) during input.
  • Prevent duplicate or blank fields for mandatory data.
User Feedback:
  • Provide error notifications during data entry (e.g., invalid ID format, duplicate entries).
Cloud Sync:
  • Ensure new registrations sync with the SW portal, BMID, and Gen IV Control Board.
Audit Reports?:
  • Log all registration events, including user details, timestamps, and entered data.

Ideally, only maintenance technicians should be able to clear a fault.   • Request Bus Access: Sends an access request to the master node when it has data to transmit.

files.contentPreview: Capacitor Used to divert high-frequency noise to ground before it can propagate through the system or back onto the power line. Capacitors in EMC filters are typically used in various configurations, such as across the line (X-capacitors) and to ground (Y-capacitors).

files.id: 9add6bfd3a35c8e4:Model/IPC !/00 Product Abstract/04 Component/EE Components/Capacitor/X Capacitor.md
files.absolutePath: /Users/spencerskelly/Documents/Vaults/Model/Model/IPC !/00 Product Abstract/04 Component/EE Components/Capacitor/X Capacitor.md
files.relativePath: Model/IPC !/00 Product Abstract/04 Component/EE Components/Capacitor/X Capacitor.md

subtypeOf: "[[Model/IPC !/00 Product Abstract/04 Component/EE Components/Capacitor/Capacitor]]"

files.contentPreview:
X Capacitor X Capacitors (across-the-line capacitors) are connected between the power lines (Line to Line or Line to Neutral) to suppress differential mode noise.
  • Provide a low-impedance path for high-frequency noise, shunting it away from the sensitive components of the EVSE.
  • Safety certified to prevent electrical hazards in case of failure.

files.id: 9add6bfd3a35c8e4:Model/IPC !/00 Product Abstract/04 Component/EE Components/Capacitor/Y Capacitor.md
files.absolutePath: /Users/spencerskelly/Documents/Vaults/Model/Model/IPC !/00 Product Abstract/04 Component/EE Components/Capacitor/Y Capacitor.md
files.relativePath: Model/IPC !/00 Product Abstract/04 Component/EE Components/Capacitor/Y Capacitor.md

subtypeOf: "[[Model/IPC !/00 Product Abstract/04 Component/EE Components/Capacitor/Capacitor]]"

files.contentPreview:
Y Capacitor Y-Capacitors (Line-to-ground capacitors) are connected between each power line and the ground (Earth) to suppress common mode noise.
  • Provide a low-impedance path for high-frequency common mode noise to be diverted to the ground, preventing it from entering or leaving the EVSE.
  • Have a higher safety rating compared to X Capacitors and are designed to fail open to prevent electrical hazards.

files.contentPreview: Choke A choke is an inductor used to block higher-frequency alternating currents while passing direct current and lower-frequency ACs in a circuit. A choke usually consists of a coil of insulated wire often wound on a magnetic core, although some consist of a doughnut-shaped ferrite bead strung on a wire.

Bulk BMID Configuration EA Note eaGUID: {6CADB900-119E-46f9-8B9B-41C78C288CE1} System Notes:
  • Cloning Functionality: The app should be able to save configuration settings from a source BMID locally within the app for later application to other BMIDs.
  • Validation Checks: The system should validate the compatibility of saved settings with the target BMID before applying changes.
  • Error Messaging: The app should provide error messages for issues encountered during cloning or application.
  • Configuration Logging: The system should log the configuration process, including:
  • Source BMID details.
  • Target BMID details.
  • Scalability: The app should
  • handle saving and applying configurations efficiently for scenarios involving large fleets.

headings: Drill Down to Faults at Company / Location / Site Level
files.contentPreview:
Drill Down to Faults at Company / Location / Site Level Goal: Narrow the view of faults/warnings to a specific org level (Company, Location, or Site) and explore relevant asset-level data for resolution or action. EA Note eaGUID: {567979D1-91D0-47a2-8846-7ACD62DA7D3E} System/Engineering Notes
  • Filters should cascade — selecting a company narrows available locations, and selecting a location narrows sites.
  • Fault/warning data refreshes every 5–10 minutes or has a manual refresh option.
  • Fault counts and visual cards should remain clickable and auto-apply context when navigating into filtered asset lists.

files.contentPreview: Authorization ineffective #2: “Unauthorized” and “Authorized” status in the asset management page does not change anything. (1/5 problem rating assuming that it is a cloud problem) 5/5 for customer satisfaction Problem statement: When a vehicle is charging and the user changes it from “Authorized” to “Unauthorized”, the charger is supposed to stop charging the vehicle. But the charger keeps on charging. This is a problem inherent to Skylink, not the Skylink kit. One of Skylink’s core value propositions is that airports can use it to 1) track energy and 2) bill for that energy. Because airports can’t currently tell who’s using their chargers or unauthorize a vehicle from charging if a customer hasn’t paid their bill, they’re effectively running a loss and giving energy away for free. This leads to strong customer dissatisfaction as they’re unable to use their product for the very purpose they purchased it for. Authorization/Unauthorization functionality does not work. files.contentPreview: Faults unreported #6: Fault not appearing under the charger status page Problem Rating 5/5. Need to raise this issue with DJ. Needs more investigation. Problem statement: When a fault is generated, for example a BMID connection lost or a temp sensor failure, the fault is not recorded in the alert report of skylink. When triggering a bmid connection lost too, the charger is supposed to show a faulted connection and stop charging. Instead, the charger will only stop charging. When creating a temp sensor fault, the fault does appear on the charger but does not stop the charge. (I believe that is normal). Seems like skylink has an issue with reporting faults. While this may not be a safety issue as our charger HW does not allow charging to occur in the event of a fault until that fault is resolved, it’s definitely an issue that our software is not picking up on any faults or recording them. files.contentPreview: Offline data loss #7: Data recovery 5/5 for customer problems 1/5 for stop shipping Problem statement: When testing the data recovery feature of the skylink kit, it seemed like the kits did not send any of the data that it had collected while the unit was offline. Expected behavior is that when the Skylink kit goes offline, the charger should still be collecting and logging the data of any charging sessions that occur. When the skylink kit returns to online status, it should grab data from the charger to capture all the charging sessions that occurred while the kit was offline, and then it should subsequently send that data to the cloud backend (Skylink) to ensure no data is lost and all data is recorded + reported. This does not currently happen. When a skylink kit goes offline and comes back online, no data is retroactively recorded in the Skylink system. files.contentPreview: Dataplicity connection failures Units are randomly going offline and losing their connection to Dataplicity, preventing remote access and monitoring. Dataplicity is critical for enabling remote management and OTA updates for units already in the field. Without being connected to it, we lose the ability to remotely access our Skylink kits, making it impossible to monitor, configure, or troubleshoot units remotely. If units are offline in Dataplicity, there is also a chance they may also fail to transmit data to Skylink, resulting in further operational blind spots; We need further investigation to confirm whether this is true. Resolution — Impact of dataplicity eaGUID: {772836A6-EE24-4fa2-AC27-1E04DE702FD8} Investigate whether Dataplicity disconnections directly impact Skylink connectivity and data transmission. files.contentPreview: Internet reconnection inconsistent #12 Device not being able to reconnect to internet Problem Statement: When a unit goes offline, it should automatically re-connect to the internet. This happens sometimes, but sometimes it doesn’t. We need to understand what the length of time a unit can be offline for before it stops attempting to reconnect automatically. It’s also inconsistent when a unit reconnects automatically. We’ve seen cases where wifi has gone out at an airport and all units were able to re-connect immediately, but we’ve seen other times where we just cycled power through a unit, but it wasn’t able to come back online. We need to understand when a Skylink kit will and will not reconnect to the internet automatically. Resolution — Resolve reconnect logic eaGUID: {FC10C940-C35C-4d01-8A86-6CF94FF50C3B} Investigate reconnect logic and implement consistent behavior.

files.contentPreview: Download Data Logs for External Analysis (Premium) Allow dataset and log count selection, validate limits, save CSV. Verify premium access. Not sure why someone would do this if they have an existing Posilink subscription, but it is a rare case that could occur where a user has a Posilink subscription, but wants to pull a CSV file with extensive log history for one individual asset. I think this is already a feature in Posilink so maybe we make the decision that we won't include this feature in the app and tell anyone with an existing Posilink subscription to use that to pull data instead.

This would be separate from the page for device connection/setup/configuration. The primary purpose of the onboarding page would be to send relevant device information to the Posicharge backend so that we can register devices in our system. Then, we'd use the app to complete the onboarding process by assigning connected devices to a network once they're registered. files.contentPreview: Create a Password/PIN to Lock Configuration EA Note eaGUID: {ABB9C00A-BE68-4d4f-B1E1-809142421EBD} Because warehouses don't often have cellular connection, maybe we could have the pin be set by an admin for an entire grouping of BMIDs EA Note eaGUID: {EB4099FC-169F-4b60-9BCE-8B3A9625867E} The user does this via a "Set Pin" button. The backend would then generate a secure PIN attached to the device and provide it to the owner (dealer). The dealer is the only user who's able to easily access this pin for future use, but the technician will not be able to see it unless they are explicitly given it by the dealer.

files.contentPreview: Apply Cloned BMID Configuration to Target BMID EA Note eaGUID: {05EDDB70-47B2-4d67-9CC8-9729647E6E87} The two fields that can't be cloned are the Battery ID and Vehicle ID. We need to make sure that cloning doesn't also copy over those parameters. In addition, we need to provide users with a reminder that they need to input the unique Battery ID and Vehicle ID, otherwise the configuration shouldn't be saved. EA Note eaGUID: {A168748A-0C5E-4bd3-A31E-60BAB10B1CB1} System should validate the compatibility of the saved settings with the target BMID. System should apply the saved configuration settings to the target BMID.

files.contentPreview:
Bulk Asset Registration (Vehicle) EA Note eaGUID: {A7D672F0-0665-462f-B193-C2E8210EA684} System Notes: Template Structure:
  • Provide a standardized template with clear instructions and mandatory/optional fields.
Data Validation:
  • Validate data during upload and generate a detailed error report for invalid rows.
  • Allow partial processing for valid rows while flagging problematic ones.
Bulk Processing Efficiency:
  • Optimize the system for large datasets (e.g., processing hundreds of assets simultaneously).
Error Handling:
  • Enable users to re-upload corrected data without overwriting already successful entries.
  • Provide error messages with suggestions for fixing invalid data.
Data Sync:
  • Sync registered assets with the cloud, Gen IV Control Board, and BMID in real-time.
Audit Logs?:
  • Log bulk reg

files.contentPreview:
Run System Diagnostics Technician initiates diagnostic tests to capture real-time system behavior. EA Note eaGUID: {5440A7D7-0A16-4a6a-9D9E-8121DD40B122} Split into power server and power stage diagnostics: Power Station:
  • DC Contactors
  • 12V Power Supply
  • 5 and 15V power supply
  • 5V to the control board
  • IGBTs
  • Power Stage PCBA (typically resistor fail)
  • Control Board Failure
  • Fuses (5A car fuses, in line car fuses, fuse on power stage)
  • Software (Re-flash SW)
Power Server:
  • Relays x3
  • Relay Board
  • Fuses
  • If main contactor fails

Access/View Fault Notification(s) To identify the presence of a fault and understand the initial details of the fault before taking further action. EA Note eaGUID: {E0999CC1-90F1-4b48-B7BD-BD54D15348E9} Note: For the display, we should have a soft reset option, where we can reset just the display without having to reset the entire charger. (i.e. Tesla touchscreen having buttons on steering wheel for soft reset) EA Note eaGUID: {3F66FAF2-0171-4c7a-8369-44C3B7CE17FF} System Notes: Fault Presentation on Display:
  • Display must show fault codes, timestamps, and basic fault descriptions clearly.
  • Include visual indicators for fault severity (color-coded alerts like red for critical, yellow for warning).
  • Provide guidance or links to troubleshooting steps (QR code linking to a troubleshooting guide).
Offline Capability
  • The fault notification system should remain operational even if the charger is not connected to the cloud.

files.contentPreview: Acknowledge/Clear Fault EA Note eaGUID: {C9CFE4D4-0D25-4a3c-BA1A-C93545375D85} If a fault is cleared, we should register when it was cleared. If we had RFID capabilities, we could also provide an audit log of who did maintenance for each fault. EA Note eaGUID: {726C586F-E144-4adf-B3D7-16B26CA51DAA} We should implement a system where our system periodically runs diagnostics on itself (checks itself). This way, if a fault was cleared or an issue was resolved by a technician, the system can auto-clear the fault status itself without requiring manual intervention. EA Note eaGUID: {126D1F81-6EFF-4936-9C95-50F756E18BBF} May want to include an option to scan a QR code to generate and send a pre-filled report to manufacturer. This way, if a technician wants to provide feedback or additional details on either a fault or resolution process, they can.

files.contentPreview:
Generate/Create Fault Report EA Note eaGUID: {8240CB21-532A-41c1-949C-CF220786D089} Mimic ProCore Edge fault logs - pulling them from the charger via the phone. - Set Date, Set Time (when fault happened), Clear Date/Time (When fault was cleared), Charger State (whether charger was equalizing, recovery charging, etc.), Battery ID, Fault Name/Description, Severity EA Note eaGUID: {029224BB-42CB-461b-B14C-C366C0275751} Create locally at the charger level - would this require an update to embedded code or could we leverage the backend? EA Note eaGUID: {B230C34A-7B76-41c7-8CEF-43D750AAEE15} System should generate a pre-filled fault report containing all captured details:
  • Fault ID, timestamp, and type.
  • Asset details (Vehicle ID, Charger ID, BMID serial number).
  • Relevant historical data (previous occurrences, operational history).
  • Software version, HW Rev/Version (Gen II vs. Gen III etc.)

headings: Generate Energy Usage Report/Summary for Single Asset
files.contentPreview:
Generate Energy Usage Report/Summary for Single Asset View the total energy usage of a single asset over a specified time period. Example: "I want to see how much energy Vehicle 123 consumed last week." EA Note eaGUID: {4F9909B1-CDCD-42c8-B60A-64C978F48CB1} System Notes Data Validation:
  • Validate the entered asset identifiers (Vehicle ID, Battery ID, BMID Serial Number) before generating the report.
Time Range Options:
  • Pre-define common time ranges (7, 14, and 30 days) for ease of use.
  • Allow custom date range input with calendar validation.
Real-Time Data Sync:
  • Ensure the report reflects the latest available data from the Gen IV Control Board and Skylink cloud.
Export Options:
  • Include support for CSV, Excel, and PDF export formats.
Error Handling:
  • Notify users when data is unavailable and why it's unavailable

  • The data should auto-refresh every 5-10 minutes or provide a “Refresh” button for manual updates.

  • Regardless of battery configuration, they are capable of handling all common passenger and cargo aircraft on the market, from the ERJ170 to the B777.

files.contentPreview: LAX_2025 A1.2.02 .D .6.. Output Amperage: The system shall be capable of providing a minimun of 200 Amps from any charge port. Actual output current provided should be intelligently determined by the need of the connected batteries. Batteries with a low state of charge shall be provided with higher current than those which have a high state of charge. Output current should only be limited by battery capacity, state of charge, temperature and the total available power for each system as described above.

files.contentPreview: 5.2: Request Version/Serial Number Command Code: 0x04, OPT, XX, CRC8 Action taken: Upon receipt of a Request Version/Serial number Command, BMID III shall read the OPT code and performs one of the following: OPT= 0 [SRS0200] Response Frame: HW_TYPE, FW_BUILD, 0x00, CRC8 BMID III shall reply with the hardware type (HW_TYPE) and firmware build (FW_BUILD). HW_TYPE = 0x0C for BMID III [SRS0210]. Note: FW_BUILD starts at 0x00 and increments with each released build. OPT=1 Response Frame: 8 ASCII characters, CRC8 BMID III shall reply with the 8-character serial number which is the lower 8 digits of the SIM ID [SRS0220]. files.contentPreview: 5.3: Request Voltage Command Code: 0x07, 0x00, XX, CRC8 Response Frame: Voltage low byte, Voltage High byte, CRC8 Action taken: Upon receipt of a Request V command, BMID III shall respond with the scaled pack voltage [SRS0230]. The high-order byte is equal to the whole volts and the low-order byte is equal to the fractional volts. Fractional volts “X” is calculated with the formula: X / 256 = fractional voltage reading. For example, a voltage of 64.37 volts would have a high byte of 0x40 (64 decimal), and a low byte of 0x5F (95 decimal). BMID3_SW_SRS

files.id: 9add6bfd3a35c8e4:Model/IPC !/03 Product Requirement/Engineering Requirements/DVS PRD/DVS PRD/2 Functional Requirements/2.2 Interface Requirements/2.2.1 Control Panel Interface/2.2.1 Control Panel Interface.md
files.absolutePath: /Users/spencerskelly/Documents/Vaults/Model/Model/IPC !/03 Product Requirement/Engineering Requirements/DVS PRD/DVS PRD/2 Functional Requirements/2.2 Interface Requirements/2.2.1 Control Panel Interface/2.2.1 Control Panel Interface.md

files.contentPreview:
2.2.1 Control Panel Interface The charger shall have two (2) Control Panels and each Control Panel shall have a control interface between the front panel control board and the regulation electronics in the charger consisting of the following control signals: Analog Current Command
  • Signal Level = 0-10V
  • DVS 100 = 0-200ADC
  • DVS 150 = 0-300ADC
Digital Enable Line
  • Signal Level = 0/5V
  • DVS 100 = Off/On
  • DVS 150 = Off/On
Analog Current Feedback
  • Signal Level = 0-10V
  • DVS 100 = 0-200ADC
  • DVS 150 = 0-300ADC
Digital Status Line
  • Signal Level = 0/5V
  • DVS 100 = Normal/Fault
  • DVS 150 = Normal/Fault
*Existing Bassi fault/status indicator lights shall be retained.

files.id: 9add6bfd3a35c8e4:Model/IPC !/03 Product Requirement/Engineering Requirements/DVS PRD/DVS PRD/2 Functional Requirements/2.2 Interface Requirements/2.2.1 Control Panel Interface/2.2.1.1 Control Power IPC Control Board.md

files.relativePath: Model/IPC !/03 Product Requirement/Engineering Requirements/DVS PRD/DVS PRD/2 Functional Requirements/2.2 Interface Requirements/2.2.1 Control Panel Interface/2.2.1.1 Control Power IPC Control Board.md
files.contentPreview: 2.2.1.1 Control Power – IPC Control Board The charger shall supply control power for the PosiCharge control board. The control power shall be routed to the front panel along with the other interfaces in the final charger configuration. The control power shall be present whenever the battery charger is turned to the “On” state. The control power shall be isolated from high voltage circuitry with UL compliant voltage isolation and shall supply the following power supply voltages and currents: +15VDC @ 2 ADC -15VDC @ 1 ADC +5VDC @ 5 ADC

files.contentPreview: 2.2.1.3 Constant-Power Regulation The PosiCharge control board shall manage the constant power functionality of the final product. The charger shall measure current and voltage operating conditions, at the output terminals, and shall adjust the current command to prevent operating conditions from exceeding the maximum specified power for the charger.

files.id: 9add6bfd3a35c8e4:Model/IPC !/03 Product Requirement/Engineering Requirements/DVS PRD/DVS PRD/2 Functional Requirements/2.2 Interface Requirements/2.2.2 Serial Interfaces.md
files.absolutePath: /Users/spencerskelly/Documents/Vaults/Model/Model/IPC !/03 Product Requirement/Engineering Requirements/DVS PRD/DVS PRD/2 Functional Requirements/2.2 Interface Requirements/2.2.2 Serial Interfaces.md
files.relativePath: Model/IPC !/03 Product Requirement/Engineering Requirements/DVS PRD/DVS PRD/2 Functional Requirements/2.2 Interface Requirements/2.2.2 Serial Interfaces.md
files.contentPreview:
2.2.2 Serial Interfaces The charger shall have the following interfaces in the final configuration:
  • BMID – Battery Monitoring and Identification
  • RS232 – Already isolated and available at front panel
  • RS422 – Requires isolation and chassis-mounted output port for use with an external RS-422 Interface device
Note: These interfaces are already a part of the PosiCharge control board but not all are isolated, as BMID does not require isolation. This specification shall be used to verify that the wiring to these interfaces is implemented in the final configuration and isolation is used where identified.

files.id: 9add6bfd3a35c8e4:Model/IPC !/03 Product Requirement/Engineering Requirements/DVS PRD/DVS PRD/2 Functional Requirements/2.2 Interface Requirements/2.2.3 Interface Isolation.md
files.absolutePath: /Users/spencerskelly/Documents/Vaults/Model/Model/IPC !/03 Product Requirement/Engineering Requirements/DVS PRD/DVS PRD/2 Functional Requirements/2.2 Interface Requirements/2.2.3 Interface Isolation.md
files.relativePath: Model/IPC !/03 Product Requirement/Engineering Requirements/DVS PRD/DVS PRD/2 Functional Requirements/2.2 Interface Requirements/2.2.3 Interface Isolation.md
files.contentPreview: 2.2.3 Interface Isolation The PosiCharge customer interfaces shall be isolated from high voltage referenced circuitry. Isolation shall be implemented in the serial interfaces to customers and between AC line voltage, ground, and output voltage. Schematics, component ratings and hi-potential testing shall be used to validate compliance.

files.id: 9add6bfd3a35c8e4:Model/IPC !/03 Product Requirement/Engineering Requirements/DVS PRD/DVS PRD/2 Functional Requirements/2.2 Interface Requirements/2.2.4 Idle shutdown for CEC- Option.md
files.absolutePath: /Users/spencerskelly/Documents/Vaults/Model/Model/IPC !/03 Product Requirement/Engineering Requirements/DVS PRD/DVS PRD/2 Functional Requirements/2.2 Interface Requirements/2.2.4 Idle shutdown for CEC- Option.md
files.relativePath: Model/IPC !/03 Product Requirement/Engineering Requirements/DVS PRD/DVS PRD/2 Functional Requirements/2.2 Interface Requirements/2.2.4 Idle shutdown for CEC- Option.md
files.contentPreview: 2.2.4 Idle shutdown for CEC- Option When this option is installed the control power shall shut off within 30 minutes when no vehicle is connected. The charger controls shall be powered for 10 minute +- 3 minutes after three-phase AC power is applied. Idle power shall be less than 10W per CEC requirements.

files.contentPreview: 2.2.5 Accessory Driver Kit The charger shall have two (2) Accessory Driver Kit interfaces installed with the required terminal block, wiring harness, and knockout used for installing stack lights, water and ventilation accessories.

files.id: 9add6bfd3a35c8e4:Model/IPC !/03 Product Requirement/Engineering Requirements/DVS PRD/DVS PRD/2 Functional Requirements/2.2 Interface Requirements/2.2.5 Accessory Driver Kit/2.2.5.1 Control Power Accessory Driver Kit.md

files.relativePath: Model/IPC !/03 Product Requirement/Engineering Requirements/DVS PRD/DVS PRD/2 Functional Requirements/2.2 Interface Requirements/2.2.5 Accessory Driver Kit/2.2.5.1 Control Power Accessory Driver Kit.md
files.contentPreview:
2.2.5.1 Control Power – Accessory Driver Kit The charger shall supply control power for the two (2) accessory driver kits. The control power shall be routed to the accessory driver kit interface. The control power shall be present whenever the battery charger is turned to the “On” state. The control power shall be capable of withstanding a short across the power with no blown fuses or damage to components. The control power shall be isolated from high voltage circuitry with UL compliant voltage isolation and shall supply the following power supply voltages and currents:
  • 24VAC @ 2A rms AC
  • Short Circuit current shall be less than 5A rms AC
  • Open Circuit voltage shall be less than 35VAC

The kit shall also be available to customers to be purchased and installed by field service personnel. This kit shall not ship as part of the baseline configuration.

files.absolutePath: /Users/spencerskelly/Documents/Vaults/Model/Model/IPC !/03 Product Requirement/Engineering Requirements/DVS PRD/DVS PRD/2 Functional Requirements/2.2 Interface Requirements/2.2.6 Optional RS-422 Interface/2.2.6.1 Control Power RS-422 Interface.md
files.relativePath: Model/IPC !/03 Product Requirement/Engineering Requirements/DVS PRD/DVS PRD/2 Functional Requirements/2.2 Interface Requirements/2.2.6 Optional RS-422 Interface/2.2.6.1 Control Power RS-422 Interface.md
files.contentPreview:
2.2.6.1 Control Power – RS-422 Interface The charger shall supply control power for two (2) optional RS-422 Interface electronics. The control power shall be routed to the interface connector along with the isolated serial communication wiring. The control power shall be present whenever the battery charger is turned to the “On” state. The control power shall be isolated from high voltage circuitry with UL compliant voltage isolation and shall supply meet the following specifications:
  • 24VAC +/- 20%
  • 0 to 500mA rms AC
  • Short Circuit and Overload Protected

files.contentPreview: 2.2.6.2 Champ Compatible Kit The DVS100 and DVS150 shall have the Champ Compatible Kit available to customers to be purchased and installed by field service personnel. This kit shall not ship as part of the baseline configuration.

files.id: 9add6bfd3a35c8e4:Model/IPC !/03 Product Requirement/Engineering Requirements/DVS PRD/DVS PRD/2 Functional Requirements/2.2 Interface Requirements/2.2.6 Optional RS-422 Interface/2.2.6.3 PosiNET Ethernet Interface.md

files.relativePath: Model/IPC !/03 Product Requirement/Engineering Requirements/DVS PRD/DVS PRD/2 Functional Requirements/2.2 Interface Requirements/2.2.6 Optional RS-422 Interface/2.2.6.3 PosiNET Ethernet Interface.md
files.contentPreview: 2.2.6.3 PosiNET – Ethernet Interface The DVS100 and DVS150 shall have the PosiNET Compatible Kit available for customers to be purchased and installed by field service personnel. PosiNET is a fleet management system for industrial electric vehicles, the data collected by the chargers are transmitted through an internal network to a remote transmission unit (RTU) which aggregates real time and historical data and passes it along secured internet connections to an offsite, back-end database system where the data is stored and analyzed. This kit shall not ship as part of the baseline configuration.

files.contentPreview: 2.3.01 Utility Voltage – North America The charger shall be designed for a nominal voltage of 480 and 600 VAC three phase input voltage as a standard voltage rating. The operating range shall be from +10% to –10% of nominal. No performance degradation shall be allowed over the operating range selected. The utility input connection will be designed as a 3-wire delta configuration.

files.contentPreview: 2.3.04 Input Connection Location – International The charger shall be supplied with 4-Conductor wire UL/CSA listed in place and ten feet (3 Meters) of cable measured from the back panel of the charger to the end of the wire. DVS 100 - The charger shall be supplied with 4-Conductor 8 AWG wire in place and ten feet (3 Meters) of cable measured from the back panel of the charger to the end of the cable. DVS 150 - The charger shall be supplied with 4-Conductor 6 AWG wire in place and ten feet (3 Meters) of cable measured from the back panel of the charger to the end of the cable.

When a condition is detected that could cause damage, the power supply shall not operate and indicate this condition through the fault line or lines.

files.contentPreview: 2.4.3.3 Current Calibration - NMS The power stage shall include a provision for calibration of current offset. This is required to ensure accurate current delivery even at currents below 10 amps.

files.relativePath: Model/IPC !/03 Product Requirement/Engineering Requirements/DVS PRD/DVS PRD/2 Functional Requirements/2.4 DC Output Requirements/2.4.4 Output Over-Voltage Withstand.md
files.contentPreview: 2.4.4 Output Over-Voltage Withstand The charger shall be capable of withstanding the connection of a 150VDC battery to the output connection without being damaged. The charger shall not attempt a charge and shall be capable of normal operation once a battery of the appropriate voltage is connected.

files.contentPreview: 2.4.5 Duty Cycle To meet the Maximum Power Rating and associated Current Range listed in section 2.4.3, 100% duty cycle shall be implemented.

files.relativePath: Model/IPC !/03 Product Requirement/Engineering Requirements/DVS PRD/DVS PRD/2 Functional Requirements/2.4 DC Output Requirements/2.4.6 Regulation Modes - NMS.md
files.contentPreview: 2.4.6 Regulation Modes - NMS The charger shall automatically perform current and voltage regulation based on the supplied command and defined voltage limit. The charger output voltage limit shall be 130VDC. If the output voltage is below 130VDC then the power supply shall regulate output current based on the current command and the power limit.

files.contentPreview: 2.4.8 Output Cable Length Two 13 ft Output Cables to be supplied with each charger. Cables shall have an Anderson Euro Connector on one end to mate to the charger and the other end is customer selectable; Anderson Euro or Schaltbau Euro.

files.contentPreview: 2.5.02 Physical Size The maximum physical size of the DVS100 and DVS150 shall be 51.47" high, 24.5" wide, and 20.44" deep.

files.contentPreview: 2.5.03 Weight The DVS100 shall weigh no more than 529Lbs and the DVS150 shall not weigh no more than 617Lbs, includes output cables.

files.id: 9add6bfd3a35c8e4:Model/IPC !/03 Product Requirement/Engineering Requirements/DVS PRD/DVS PRD/2 Functional Requirements/2.5 Mechanical Requirements/2.5.04 Factory Environment.md

files.relativePath: Model/IPC !/03 Product Requirement/Engineering Requirements/DVS PRD/DVS PRD/2 Functional Requirements/2.5 Mechanical Requirements/2.5.04 Factory Environment.md
files.contentPreview: 2.5.04 Factory Environment The charger shall operate with standard characteristics when operated in a typical factory environment. The target environment typically has contamination from welding processes, metal foundry processes, and fabrication activities and may include conductive fibers or dust accumulation. Service and maintenance procedures to maintain standard characteristics are acceptable. EA Note eaGUID: {A12FB425-005A-4e6e-ABE4-487EA56C9610} Need equivalent information for PCE25.

files.id: 9add6bfd3a35c8e4:Model/IPC !/03 Product Requirement/Engineering Requirements/DVS PRD/DVS PRD/2 Functional Requirements/2.5 Mechanical Requirements/2.5.05 Color and Finish.md

files.relativePath: Model/IPC !/03 Product Requirement/Engineering Requirements/DVS PRD/DVS PRD/2 Functional Requirements/2.5 Mechanical Requirements/2.5.05 Color and Finish.md
files.contentPreview: 2.5.05 Color and Finish The charger shall be supplied with a powder coat finish. The finish shall be CORVEL TGIC POLYESTERS ANSI 70 GREY, 30-7065, GLOSS:60-70-U.L. Also, available orange color cabinet option Pantone 1665 / RAL2004 (CMYK C:0 M:73 Y:100 K:0).

files.id: 9add6bfd3a35c8e4:Model/IPC !/03 Product Requirement/Engineering Requirements/DVS PRD/DVS PRD/2 Functional Requirements/2.5 Mechanical Requirements/2.5.06 PosiCharge Logo.md
files.absolutePath: /Users/spencerskelly/Documents/Vaults/Model/Model/IPC !/03 Product Requirement/Engineering Requirements/DVS PRD/DVS PRD/2 Functional Requirements/2.5 Mechanical Requirements/2.5.06 PosiCharge Logo.md
files.relativePath: Model/IPC !/03 Product Requirement/Engineering Requirements/DVS PRD/DVS PRD/2 Functional Requirements/2.5 Mechanical Requirements/2.5.06 PosiCharge Logo.md
files.contentPreview: 2.5.06 PosiCharge Logo The charger shall be supplied with a PosiCharge logo sticker per PosiCharge design documents that shall be affixed to the charger at the time of manufacture. The location of the sticker shall be on the top right corner of Control Panel Assembly “A”.

files.id: 9add6bfd3a35c8e4:Model/IPC !/03 Product Requirement/Engineering Requirements/DVS PRD/DVS PRD/2 Functional Requirements/2.5 Mechanical Requirements/2.5.07 PosiCharge Front Panel.md
files.absolutePath: /Users/spencerskelly/Documents/Vaults/Model/Model/IPC !/03 Product Requirement/Engineering Requirements/DVS PRD/DVS PRD/2 Functional Requirements/2.5 Mechanical Requirements/2.5.07 PosiCharge Front Panel.md
files.relativePath: Model/IPC !/03 Product Requirement/Engineering Requirements/DVS PRD/DVS PRD/2 Functional Requirements/2.5 Mechanical Requirements/2.5.07 PosiCharge Front Panel.md
files.contentPreview: 2.5.07 PosiCharge Front Panel The charger shall feature two Bassi regulation boards and two Posicharge front panel assemblies. The Control Panel for Port A is to be mounted above the Control Panel for Port B. A label “A” is to be located on the left side of Port A Control Panel Assembly. A Label “B” is to be located on the right side of Port B Control Panel Assembly.

files.id: 9add6bfd3a35c8e4:Model/IPC !/03 Product Requirement/Engineering Requirements/DVS PRD/DVS PRD/2 Functional Requirements/2.5 Mechanical Requirements/2.5.08 Fused Disconnect Mounting Option N - A.md
files.absolutePath: /Users/spencerskelly/Documents/Vaults/Model/Model/IPC !/03 Product Requirement/Engineering Requirements/DVS PRD/DVS PRD/2 Functional Requirements/2.5 Mechanical Requirements/2.5.08 Fused Disconnect Mounting Option N - A.md

files.basename: 2.5.08 Fused Disconnect Mounting Option N - A
files.contentPreview: 2.5.08 Fused Disconnect Mounting Option – N/A The charger shall support an optional fused disconnect which can be ordered at the time of manufacture. This option may be implemented using either a fused-disconnect assembly or remotely activated relay assembly. Either option shall preclude entry into the charger when in the operate switch position.

files.id: 9add6bfd3a35c8e4:Model/IPC !/03 Product Requirement/Engineering Requirements/DVS PRD/DVS PRD/2 Functional Requirements/2.5 Mechanical Requirements/2.5.09 Accessory Driver Kit.md
files.absolutePath: /Users/spencerskelly/Documents/Vaults/Model/Model/IPC !/03 Product Requirement/Engineering Requirements/DVS PRD/DVS PRD/2 Functional Requirements/2.5 Mechanical Requirements/2.5.09 Accessory Driver Kit.md
files.relativePath: Model/IPC !/03 Product Requirement/Engineering Requirements/DVS PRD/DVS PRD/2 Functional Requirements/2.5 Mechanical Requirements/2.5.09 Accessory Driver Kit.md
files.contentPreview: 2.5.09 Accessory Driver Kit The charger shall have two (2) Accessory Driver Kits installed with the required terminal block, wiring harness, and knockout used for installing stack lights, water and ventilation accessories.

files.id: 9add6bfd3a35c8e4:Model/IPC !/03 Product Requirement/Engineering Requirements/DVS PRD/DVS PRD/2 Functional Requirements/2.5 Mechanical Requirements/2.5.10 External RS-422 Interface Option.md
files.absolutePath: /Users/spencerskelly/Documents/Vaults/Model/Model/IPC !/03 Product Requirement/Engineering Requirements/DVS PRD/DVS PRD/2 Functional Requirements/2.5 Mechanical Requirements/2.5.10 External RS-422 Interface Option.md
files.relativePath: Model/IPC !/03 Product Requirement/Engineering Requirements/DVS PRD/DVS PRD/2 Functional Requirements/2.5 Mechanical Requirements/2.5.10 External RS-422 Interface Option.md
files.contentPreview: 2.5.10 External RS-422 Interface Option The charger shall support a mounting location and provisions for mounting an optional external RS-422 Interface device. In addition to the mounting of the RS-422 Interface device, mounting provisions for the Serial Isolation device, and a connector location shall also be supported.

files.id: 9add6bfd3a35c8e4:Model/IPC !/03 Product Requirement/Engineering Requirements/DVS PRD/DVS PRD/2 Functional Requirements/2.5 Mechanical Requirements/2.5.11 Pogo-Stick Mounting Option N - A.md

files.relativePath: Model/IPC !/03 Product Requirement/Engineering Requirements/DVS PRD/DVS PRD/2 Functional Requirements/2.5 Mechanical Requirements/2.5.11 Pogo-Stick Mounting Option N - A.md
files.contentPreview: 2.5.11 Pogo-Stick Mounting Option – N/A The charger shall support a mounting location and provisions for mounting an optional pogo stick for cable management on the exterior of the charger.

files.id: 9add6bfd3a35c8e4:Model/IPC !/03 Product Requirement/Engineering Requirements/DVS PRD/DVS PRD/2 Functional Requirements/2.5 Mechanical Requirements/2.5.12 Shipping Container.md

files.contentPreview: 2.5.12 Shipping Container The charger shall be packaged in a shipping container suitable for optimization of packing density for overseas shipment. Details of shipping configuration to be mutually agreed between Posicharge and Bassi. EA Note eaGUID: {F96D0DF0-AED5-43f9-A3BC-D8C338479887} Follow PC Edge requirements

files.id: 9add6bfd3a35c8e4:Model/IPC !/03 Product Requirement/Engineering Requirements/DVS PRD/DVS PRD/2 Functional Requirements/2.5 Mechanical Requirements/2.5.13 Installation Stacking N - A.md

files.relativePath: Model/IPC !/03 Product Requirement/Engineering Requirements/DVS PRD/DVS PRD/2 Functional Requirements/2.5 Mechanical Requirements/2.5.13 Installation Stacking N - A.md
files.contentPreview: 2.5.13 Installation Stacking – N/A The charger shall be capable of stacking two high at the time of installation. This is to facilitate better utilization of factory floor space. This requirement can be implemented using a kit and external frame approach. The requirement shall be implemented as a product option available to customers at the time of purchase. EA Note eaGUID: {29671031-6C46-4739-83BA-AC20295DE656} Two PCE25 10B cannot be installed one on the top of the other.

files.id: 9add6bfd3a35c8e4:Model/IPC !/03 Product Requirement/Engineering Requirements/DVS PRD/DVS PRD/2 Functional Requirements/2.5 Mechanical Requirements/2.5.14 Installation Area N - A.md

files.contentPreview: 2.5.14 Installation Area – N/A The DVS100 / DVS150 shall support a wall mount installation. All cooling shall be achieved either through the front panel or the side panels. EA Note eaGUID: {B4D73025-3562-4522-A53C-B7CE823D5EDE} Need equivalent requirements for the PCE25

files.id: 9add6bfd3a35c8e4:Model/IPC !/03 Product Requirement/Engineering Requirements/DVS PRD/DVS PRD/2 Functional Requirements/2.5 Mechanical Requirements/2.5.15 Forklift Handling.md

files.id: 9add6bfd3a35c8e4:Model/IPC !/03 Product Requirement/Engineering Requirements/DVS PRD/DVS PRD/2 Functional Requirements/2.5 Mechanical Requirements/2.5.16 Safety Ground Connection.md

files.contentPreview: 2.5.16 Safety Ground Connection The charger shall have provision for making a ground connection that meets the requirements of UL and NEC.

files.id: 9add6bfd3a35c8e4:Model/IPC !/03 Product Requirement/Engineering Requirements/DVS PRD/DVS PRD/2 Functional Requirements/2.5 Mechanical Requirements/2.5.17 Mean Time to Repair.md

files.contentPreview: 2.5.17 Mean Time to Repair The MTTR of the DVS100 and DVS150 shall be 30 minutes, when completed by a single trained field service technician or PosiCharge certified forklift shop mechanic. EA Note eaGUID: {A12FB425-005A-4e6e-ABE4-487EA56C9610} Need equivalent information for PCE25. EA Note eaGUID: {84CF979D-2787-4ccf-BC50-DC6EC0FB235E} Equivalent requirements for the PC25 are needed.

files.id: 9add6bfd3a35c8e4:Model/IPC !/03 Product Requirement/Engineering Requirements/DVS PRD/DVS PRD/2 Functional Requirements/2.5 Mechanical Requirements/2.5.18 Easily replaceable Internal Components.md

files.contentPreview: 2.5.18 Easily replaceable Internal Components The DVS100 and DVS150 shall, be designed with easy access to internal components. All major field-replaceable units that carry voltage (Ex. Power stage, control board) shall indicate failure by means of an LED or visible fault indicator. EA Note eaGUID: {84CF979D-2787-4ccf-BC50-DC6EC0FB235E} Equivalent requirements for the PC25 are needed.

Design for manufacturing shall be coordinated with manufacturing and this requirement shall be met by approval from the manufacturing engineer at the producibility review. EA Note eaGUID: {84CF979D-2787-4ccf-BC50-DC6EC0FB235E} Equivalent requirements for the PC25 are needed. EA Note eaGUID: {89B8B08F-B4F3-451e-917F-21FA2FE2F9DC} Needs equivalent requirement for PC25

files.absolutePath: /Users/spencerskelly/Documents/Vaults/Model/Model/IPC !/03 Product Requirement/Engineering Requirements/DVS PRD/DVS PRD/2 Functional Requirements/2.6 Agency - Reliability Requirements/2.6.10 Input Voltage Mismatch.md
files.relativePath: Model/IPC !/03 Product Requirement/Engineering Requirements/DVS PRD/DVS PRD/2 Functional Requirements/2.6 Agency - Reliability Requirements/2.6.10 Input Voltage Mismatch.md
files.contentPreview: 2.6.10 Input Voltage Mismatch A product that is intended for operation with two or more supply-voltage levels or with a varying number of battery cells or both, shall be connected in such a way as to produce the most adverse conditions when connected to the highest alternating-current input voltage specified for the charger. For example, 600 volts plus 10 percent on a 480-volt tap with the product connected for 12-cell charging to a eight-cell battery. The product is to be connected to a discharged battery, all normally supplied protective devices are to be left in the circuit, and the product is then to be energized. The test is to be continued until the internal protection opens, constant temperatures are attained, or the circuitry opens. If an automatically reset protector is provided, the test is to be continued for 7 hours. A manually reset protector is to be operated for 50 cycles.

files.contentPreview: 2.6.11 Short Circuit The DVS100 and DVS150 shall be designed to withstand an output short circuit during normal operation at full load. The DVS100 and DVS150 shall successfully recover upon removal of short circuit condition.

files.id: 9add6bfd3a35c8e4:Model/IPC !/03 Product Requirement/Engineering Requirements/DVS PRD/DVS PRD/2 Functional Requirements/2.6 Agency - Reliability Requirements/2.6.12 Reverse Battery.md

files.relativePath: Model/IPC !/03 Product Requirement/Engineering Requirements/DVS PRD/DVS PRD/2 Functional Requirements/2.6 Agency - Reliability Requirements/2.6.12 Reverse Battery.md
files.contentPreview: 2.6.12 Reverse Battery The DVS100 and DVS150 charger shall be capable of withstanding reverse connection of battery voltage to 150VDC. The charger shall not be damaged due to reverse wiring errors in the output power cables or connectors. Upon correction of the wiring errors the power supply shall resume charging.

files.id: 9add6bfd3a35c8e4:Model/IPC !/03 Product Requirement/Engineering Requirements/DVS PRD/DVS PRD/2 Functional Requirements/2.6 Agency - Reliability Requirements/2.6.13 Anti-Arcing Specification.md
files.absolutePath: /Users/spencerskelly/Documents/Vaults/Model/Model/IPC !/03 Product Requirement/Engineering Requirements/DVS PRD/DVS PRD/2 Functional Requirements/2.6 Agency - Reliability Requirements/2.6.13 Anti-Arcing Specification.md
files.relativePath: Model/IPC !/03 Product Requirement/Engineering Requirements/DVS PRD/DVS PRD/2 Functional Requirements/2.6 Agency - Reliability Requirements/2.6.13 Anti-Arcing Specification.md
files.contentPreview: 2.6.13 Anti-Arcing Specification The charger interface shall support rapid shut down to prevent connector anti-arcing. From loss of Pilot to output current below 5 ADC shall be 15 milli-seconds or less. The shut down can be implemented via the current command or digital enable line. Note:The PosiCharge control board takes 5 milli-seconds to process the pilot signal.

files.contentPreview: 2.6.15 Emergency Power Off (EPO) The function of the EPO switch is to quickly disconnect both the AC and DC power circuits. The charger shall provide an EPO switch operation. After an Emergency Power Off the EPO switch is manually reset by pulling and latching, the charger shall not turn “On” until the “Restart” button is pressed or power has been recycled (On/Off). EA Note eaGUID: {A9F7AFF5-94AE-4d60-B576-9DC65CC972CE} The PC Edge has a "Stop" Push button not an EPO.

files.relativePath: Model/IPC !/03 Product Requirement/Engineering Requirements/DVS PRD/DVS PRD/2 Functional Requirements/2.6 Agency - Reliability Requirements/2.6.16 Humidity Pre-Conditioning before Hipot - NMS.md
files.contentPreview: 2.6.16 Humidity Pre-Conditioning before Hipot - NMS A product shall be conditioned for 24 hours in moist air having a relative humidity of 85±5 percent at a temperature of 32.0 ±2.0°C (89.6 ±3.6°F). Hipot perform after the conditioning: A product other than as mentioned in (a) shall have an insulation resistance of 50,000 ohms or more between live parts and interconnected dead metal parts.

files.contentPreview: GSE_SW 1.1 Purpose The PowerStation is one of two primary components of the AeroVironment Dual Vehicle Charging Systems (DVS) and the Multiple Vehicle Charging Systems (MVS). These systems provide fast charging technology and intelligent power management for charging multiple vehicles. The three primary components of the systems are the PowerServer, the PowerStation and the Battery Monitor/Identification (BMID) unit. The PowerServer functions as the utility line rectifier, converting the 3-phase power to DC power for the PowerStations. In the original MVS, up to 5 dual-port PowerStations, can be connected in a daisy chain manner to the DC bus of a single Communications (Comm) PowerServer, allowing up to 10 vehicles to charge simultaneously. In the NGPS MVS System up to 8 dual-port PowerStations can be connected to the DC bus, allowing p to 16 vehicles to charge simultaneously. files.contentPreview: GSE_SW 2.1 User Interface The user interface processes inputs from the analog-to-digital converter driver, BMID handler, charge handler, charge log handler, fault handler, fault log handler, LED driver, RTC handler, and system state handler. Status information is output to the user display, LEDs and serial port. User requests for data, via the serial port, are also processed by the user interface.

The UD screens are accessed and navigated through, and data is entered and modified, via the use of the front panel buttons.

files.contentPreview: GSE_SW 2.2 Charge Handling The charge handler is designed to implement an AV standard industrial Fast Charge algorithm. This is based on a typical Constant Current - Constant Voltage - Constant Current profile with provisions to maximize fast charge performance and battery life. In addition to Fast Charging, the system will also provide a means to Equalize a battery. The steps involved with charging are broken into charge states: Idle, Fast Charge, Full, Equalization Charge and Abnormal Termination states. These states apply to both Port A and Port B.

files.contentPreview: GSE_SW 2.2.1 Charger States The charge handler implements a standard charge protocol by progressing from one state to another using transition checks along the way. The charge state mapping is shown in Figure 2-3. The data for the charging algorithms comes from four places: the BMID attached to the battery (Battery configuration, voltage and temperature), the charger inputs (current, voltage and connection status), the charger configuration parameters, and the charging tables (see [11]). The request to charge comes from the system state machine. Once started, the charging handler progresses through the charging states until it terminates either normally or abnormally. The first states of charging are for charge initialization. By default, if no charge is requested the system waits in the Disconnected state. files.contentPreview: GSE_SW 2.3 Fault Handling The fault handler collects, filters, and processes errors into either warnings or faults. The fault handler is used to implement hysterisis on system errors that come from external handlers. Some errors that are considered fatal will set faults and never clear, while others will clear themselves as soon as the cause for the error condition ceases.

files.contentPreview: GSE_SW 2.4 Communications The charger communicates to the outside world through the use of the Diagnostic Port and to the BMID through the Data Lines. The Diagnostic port serves multiple purposes: transmitting data, receiving user commands and uploading application software to Master and Slave PowerStations. The BMID Data Lines are the charger’s link to the BMID. Through these Lines the charger is able to write new data to the BMID as well as receive critical parameters that are used to ensure efficient charging.

files.contentPreview: GSE_SW 2.4.2 BMID communications The BMID is a variety of the SmartGuard (SG). It varies from other SmartGuards in that only one BMID can be attached to the SmartGuard bus at a time. This is not due to any electrical characteristics, but due to the BMID command protocol. The charger requires the use of a Battery Monitor/Identifier (BMID) to monitor the battery during charge and allow the charger to track the equalization schedule and charge history of each pack. Each BMID has an optically isolated two-wire communication bus with which to communicate. The bus has two possible modes, Command and Response

files.contentPreview: GSE_SW 2.4.4 PowerServer Communications (MVS) The MVS system uses two distinct types of PowerServers. The first is the Comm PowerServer, which communicates with the Master PowerStation over an RS422 link. The second is the Next Generation PowerServer (NGPS), which is controlled by the Master PowerStation via two relays.

files.contentPreview: GSE_SW 2.4.3.1 PowerStation Communications In an MVS system, the Master PowerStation and Slave PowerStations are linked together to allow the Master to monitor all network traffic. The Master performs a system monitoring function that allocates the available power from the PowerServer to the ports. Each PowerStation has two network communication channels. The network consists of both transmit and receive pairs between nodes. By wiring the RX and TX pairs from one PowerStation to the TX and RX pairs of the next there will be a full duplex link between each.

files.contentPreview: GSE_SW 2.7.1 Watering The MVS/DVS system provides a means of controlling an external watering system to support battery maintenance. The system includes controlling pre-defined systems, as well as offering a custom mode to control systems not currently defined in the system. Watering is accomplished during EQ charging as configured in the Charger Configuration Watering Control Menu (see section 2.8.1.2.11). The charger’s watering functionality includes enabling a relay to control the external watering system, for a configured duration, at the appropriate time during the EQ charge.

files.contentPreview: GSE_SW 2.7.2 External Charge Control A minimal implementation of the External Charge Control (see 2.8.1.2.16) feature is available in the system. This feature allows an external signal to command the system to a low power mode. When the external signal is enabled and activated, all charging is stopped.

files.contentPreview: GSE_SW 2.9 PosiNET Software Requirements The charger broadcasts real time data for collection and processing by an external resource, such as a stand-alone PC. The broadcast data consists of charger and BMID real-time data. The charger also transmits log data when requested by an external resource. The Master PowerStation can be configured to collects log data from it’s own activities as well as from all Slave PowerStations in the networked system. The log data consists of the charge events, fault events and BMID data collected by the charger (see section 2.6).

headings: GSE_SW 2.9.3.1 Selector Mode [Not implemented at this time]
files.contentPreview: GSE_SW 2.9.3.1 Selector Mode [Not implemented at this time] The Selector Mode is used to provide the capability to command the charger, via the serial communication port, to open and close relays on the charger control board. The relays can be used to control external accessories, such as lights. One example of the use of Selector Mode is the Truck Selector. In the Truck Selector application, Selector Mode is used to support turning a green or red light on to indicate which trucks are charged to a sufficient SOC for use, and which are not. The external system commands the charger to illuminate the green light and extinguish the red light for the trucks that are ready for use. The external system commands the charger to illuminate the red light and extinguish the green light for trucks that need to remain charging. All decision making is performed external to the charger.

files.contentPreview: 2.1.2 Reduced Power Capability The MVS Server shall have a nameplate power code. This power code shall not contain any intelligent data but shall be randomly generated. The power code shall indicate a rating that is used in the Master Power Server in the same system and shall be used to set the power rating for the system. The codes for power rating shall be TBD.

files.id: 9add6bfd3a35c8e4:Model/IPC !/03 Product Requirement/Engineering Requirements/MVS PRD/MVS PRD/2 Functional Requirements/2.1 System Level Requirements/2.1.3 Backward Compatibility.md
files.absolutePath: /Users/spencerskelly/Documents/Vaults/Model/Model/IPC !/03 Product Requirement/Engineering Requirements/MVS PRD/MVS PRD/2 Functional Requirements/2.1 System Level Requirements/2.1.3 Backward Compatibility.md
files.relativePath: Model/IPC !/03 Product Requirement/Engineering Requirements/MVS PRD/MVS PRD/2 Functional Requirements/2.1 System Level Requirements/2.1.3 Backward Compatibility.md
files.contentPreview:
2.1.3 Backward Compatibility The MVS Server shall be compatible with existing installations using the previous generation server. The changes allowable to the system to facilitate this shall be limited to:
  • Replacement of the MVS Station(s) software.
  • Addition of an accessory driver board.
  • MVS Server power ratings must match.
Verification of this requirement shall be met by installation in an existing sight, by trained field-service personnel, with the changes allowed.

files.id: 9add6bfd3a35c8e4:Model/IPC !/03 Product Requirement/Engineering Requirements/MVS PRD/MVS PRD/2 Functional Requirements/2.1 System Level Requirements/2.1.5 Efficiency Requirement.md
files.absolutePath: /Users/spencerskelly/Documents/Vaults/Model/Model/IPC !/03 Product Requirement/Engineering Requirements/MVS PRD/MVS PRD/2 Functional Requirements/2.1 System Level Requirements/2.1.5 Efficiency Requirement.md
files.relativePath: Model/IPC !/03 Product Requirement/Engineering Requirements/MVS PRD/MVS PRD/2 Functional Requirements/2.1 System Level Requirements/2.1.5 Efficiency Requirement.md
files.contentPreview: 2.1.5 Efficiency Requirement The MVS Server shall have a measured efficiency of greater than ninety percent at loads greater than fifty percent of rating. Test conditions shall be at nominal line and load conditions. The efficiency shall be measured from the AC input terminals to the DC output terminals.

files.id: 9add6bfd3a35c8e4:Model/IPC !/03 Product Requirement/Engineering Requirements/MVS PRD/MVS PRD/2 Functional Requirements/2.2 Input Specification/2.2.1 Rated Voltage Range.md
files.absolutePath: /Users/spencerskelly/Documents/Vaults/Model/Model/IPC !/03 Product Requirement/Engineering Requirements/MVS PRD/MVS PRD/2 Functional Requirements/2.2 Input Specification/2.2.1 Rated Voltage Range.md
files.relativePath: Model/IPC !/03 Product Requirement/Engineering Requirements/MVS PRD/MVS PRD/2 Functional Requirements/2.2 Input Specification/2.2.1 Rated Voltage Range.md
files.contentPreview: 2.2.1 Rated Voltage Range The input rated voltage shall be 480 VAC and 600 VAC. The MVS Server shall be designed for configuration at either voltage as a nominal value. The tolerance for input voltage shall be plus ten percent to minus fifteen percent as a nominal range. No performance degradation shall be allowed over this operating range.

files.contentPreview: 2.2.4 Harmonic Distortion Measured harmonic distortion shall be less than twenty five percent at nominal output load and input voltage.

files.id: 9add6bfd3a35c8e4:Model/IPC !/03 Product Requirement/Engineering Requirements/MVS PRD/MVS PRD/2 Functional Requirements/2.2 Input Specification/2.2.5 Operating Frequency.md

files.contentPreview: 2.2.5 Operating Frequency The MVS Server shall be compatible with sixty-Hertz utilities. All performance testing shall be conducted at sixty Hertz.

files.absolutePath: /Users/spencerskelly/Documents/Vaults/Model/Model/IPC !/03 Product Requirement/Engineering Requirements/MVS PRD/MVS PRD/2 Functional Requirements/2.3 Output Specification/2.3.1 Rated Output Voltage Range.md
files.relativePath: Model/IPC !/03 Product Requirement/Engineering Requirements/MVS PRD/MVS PRD/2 Functional Requirements/2.3 Output Specification/2.3.1 Rated Output Voltage Range.md
files.contentPreview: 2.3.1 Rated Output Voltage Range The minimum DC output voltage shall be 137 volts DC. The maximum DC output voltage shall be 170 volts DC. The minimum voltage shall be measured under a low line condition at full load. The maximum voltage shall be measured at ten percent load at maximum line.

files.contentPreview: 2.3.2 DC Output Monitoring The DC output voltage shall not be monitored for faults or operability. A Pre-charge lockout shall prevent damage from occurring to the server or stations when inadequate time is given for pre-charge to complete. The lockout function shall be verified by observing that the output current does not exceed the rated output current when the maximum specified number of stations are connected and all enables are applied simultaneously.

files.id: 9add6bfd3a35c8e4:Model/IPC !/03 Product Requirement/Engineering Requirements/MVS PRD/MVS PRD/2 Functional Requirements/2.3 Output Specification/2.3.3 Fault Tolerance.md
files.absolutePath: /Users/spencerskelly/Documents/Vaults/Model/Model/IPC !/03 Product Requirement/Engineering Requirements/MVS PRD/MVS PRD/2 Functional Requirements/2.3 Output Specification/2.3.3 Fault Tolerance.md
files.relativePath: Model/IPC !/03 Product Requirement/Engineering Requirements/MVS PRD/MVS PRD/2 Functional Requirements/2.3 Output Specification/2.3.3 Fault Tolerance.md
files.contentPreview: 2.3.3 Fault Tolerance The MVS Server shall be capable of withstanding faults applied as a result of wiring errors introduced during installation. An external and Operating-Manual-specified circuit breaker is mandatory for this testing. Resetting of this external circuit breaker shall be allowed to restart the unit. The faults shall be applied for a minimum of one second to verify this requirement. A failed component shall not be allowed during this test.

files.id: 9add6bfd3a35c8e4:Model/IPC !/03 Product Requirement/Engineering Requirements/MVS PRD/MVS PRD/2 Functional Requirements/2.3 Output Specification/2.3.5 Output Current.md

files.contentPreview: 2.3.5 Output Current Maximum current will occur at the minimum specified line condition. At this condition the MVS Server shall be capable of supplying the full specified power.

files.id: 9add6bfd3a35c8e4:Model/IPC !/03 Product Requirement/Engineering Requirements/MVS PRD/MVS PRD/2 Functional Requirements/2.3 Output Specification/2.3.6 Output Ripple Current.md
files.absolutePath: /Users/spencerskelly/Documents/Vaults/Model/Model/IPC !/03 Product Requirement/Engineering Requirements/MVS PRD/MVS PRD/2 Functional Requirements/2.3 Output Specification/2.3.6 Output Ripple Current.md
files.relativePath: Model/IPC !/03 Product Requirement/Engineering Requirements/MVS PRD/MVS PRD/2 Functional Requirements/2.3 Output Specification/2.3.6 Output Ripple Current.md
files.contentPreview: 2.3.6 Output Ripple Current The MVS Server shall have no more than ten percent ripple. Ripple shall be measured as the AC RMS component divided by the DC output current. These measurements shall be made at nominal load and line conditions.

files.id: 9add6bfd3a35c8e4:Model/IPC !/03 Product Requirement/Engineering Requirements/MVS PRD/MVS PRD/2 Functional Requirements/2.4 Agency And Reliability Requirements/2.4.1 Safety Agency Approval.md

files.contentPreview: 2.4.1 Safety Agency Approval The MVS Server shall be listed under the UL specification UL1012 Power Supplies at 480 VAC input. The MVS Server shall also be approved under the CSA (cUL) specification CSA22.2 no. 107, at 480 and 600 VAC input

files.contentPreview: 2.4.2 FMEA The MVS Server shall be analyzed using standard FMEA methods. The FMEA results shall be communicated to the design team in a formal review.

files.contentPreview: 2.4.3 Sags, Surges, and Strikes The MVS Server shall be designed and tested for compliance with UL991.

files.id: 9add6bfd3a35c8e4:Model/IPC !/03 Product Requirement/Engineering Requirements/MVS PRD/MVS PRD/2 Functional Requirements/2.4 Agency And Reliability Requirements/2.4.4 Thermal Monitoring.md
files.absolutePath: /Users/spencerskelly/Documents/Vaults/Model/Model/IPC !/03 Product Requirement/Engineering Requirements/MVS PRD/MVS PRD/2 Functional Requirements/2.4 Agency And Reliability Requirements/2.4.4 Thermal Monitoring.md
files.relativePath: Model/IPC !/03 Product Requirement/Engineering Requirements/MVS PRD/MVS PRD/2 Functional Requirements/2.4 Agency And Reliability Requirements/2.4.4 Thermal Monitoring.md
files.contentPreview: 2.4.4 Thermal Monitoring MVS Server shall include sensors on all magnetic components and semiconductors and shall disable operation of the MVS Server if these temperatures are above the design rating. No other protective monitoring shall be included in the MVS Server.

files.id: 9add6bfd3a35c8e4:Model/IPC !/03 Product Requirement/Engineering Requirements/MVS PRD/MVS PRD/2 Functional Requirements/2.4 Agency And Reliability Requirements/2.4.5 Isolation.md
