files.relativePath: Model/IPC !/03 Product Requirement/Engineering Requirements/MVS PRD/MVS PRD/2 Functional Requirements/2.4 Agency And Reliability Requirements/2.4.5 Isolation.md
files.contentPreview: 2.4.5 Isolation The MVS Server shall include a dielectric isolation barrier. The isolation barrier shall comply with the designated UL and cUL requirements for this type of barrier.

files.id: 9add6bfd3a35c8e4:Model/IPC !/03 Product Requirement/Engineering Requirements/MVS PRD/MVS PRD/2 Functional Requirements/2.4 Agency And Reliability Requirements/2.4.6 Mean Time Between Failures.md
files.absolutePath: /Users/spencerskelly/Documents/Vaults/Model/Model/IPC !/03 Product Requirement/Engineering Requirements/MVS PRD/MVS PRD/2 Functional Requirements/2.4 Agency And Reliability Requirements/2.4.6 Mean Time Between Failures.md
files.relativePath: Model/IPC !/03 Product Requirement/Engineering Requirements/MVS PRD/MVS PRD/2 Functional Requirements/2.4 Agency And Reliability Requirements/2.4.6 Mean Time Between Failures.md
files.contentPreview: 2.4.6 Mean Time Between Failures The MTBF shall be a minimum of twenty thousand hours. The MTBF shall be verified by MIL-Handbook-217 method.

files.id: 9add6bfd3a35c8e4:Model/IPC !/03 Product Requirement/Engineering Requirements/MVS PRD/MVS PRD/2 Functional Requirements/2.5 Mechanical Requirements/2.5.1 Physical Size Constraint.md
files.absolutePath: /Users/spencerskelly/Documents/Vaults/Model/Model/IPC !/03 Product Requirement/Engineering Requirements/MVS PRD/MVS PRD/2 Functional Requirements/2.5 Mechanical Requirements/2.5.1 Physical Size Constraint.md
files.relativePath: Model/IPC !/03 Product Requirement/Engineering Requirements/MVS PRD/MVS PRD/2 Functional Requirements/2.5 Mechanical Requirements/2.5.1 Physical Size Constraint.md
files.contentPreview: 2.5.1 Physical Size Constraint The maximum physical size of the MVS Server shall be 60" high, 42" wide, and 27" deep. The maximum buildup of the MVS Server from the wall surface shall be thirty inches. This shall include any protruding lamps or switch assemblies.

files.id: 9add6bfd3a35c8e4:Model/IPC !/03 Product Requirement/Engineering Requirements/MVS PRD/MVS PRD/2 Functional Requirements/2.5 Mechanical Requirements/2.5.2 Paint Requirement.md
files.absolutePath: /Users/spencerskelly/Documents/Vaults/Model/Model/IPC !/03 Product Requirement/Engineering Requirements/MVS PRD/MVS PRD/2 Functional Requirements/2.5 Mechanical Requirements/2.5.2 Paint Requirement.md
files.relativePath: Model/IPC !/03 Product Requirement/Engineering Requirements/MVS PRD/MVS PRD/2 Functional Requirements/2.5 Mechanical Requirements/2.5.2 Paint Requirement.md
files.contentPreview: 2.5.2 Paint Requirement The MVS Server shall be power coated on TBD surfaces. The paint shall be Corvel TGIC Polysters ANSI 70 GRAY, 30-7065, GLOSS:60-70-U.L.

files.id: 9add6bfd3a35c8e4:Model/IPC !/03 Product Requirement/Engineering Requirements/MVS PRD/MVS PRD/2 Functional Requirements/2.5 Mechanical Requirements/2.5.3 Installation Limitation.md
files.absolutePath: /Users/spencerskelly/Documents/Vaults/Model/Model/IPC !/03 Product Requirement/Engineering Requirements/MVS PRD/MVS PRD/2 Functional Requirements/2.5 Mechanical Requirements/2.5.3 Installation Limitation.md
files.relativePath: Model/IPC !/03 Product Requirement/Engineering Requirements/MVS PRD/MVS PRD/2 Functional Requirements/2.5 Mechanical Requirements/2.5.3 Installation Limitation.md
files.contentPreview: 2.5.3 Installation Limitation The MVS Server shall be designed for installation distances as short as six inches from one side (either), and the rear of the unit. EA Note eaGUID: {7B366632-DDA8-44ea-B073-00A24844801C} Need equivalent Installation Limitations for PCE25. Follow PC Edge installation recomendations.

files.id: 9add6bfd3a35c8e4:Model/IPC !/03 Product Requirement/Engineering Requirements/MVS PRD/MVS PRD/2 Functional Requirements/2.5 Mechanical Requirements/2.5.4 Mean Time To Service.md
files.absolutePath: /Users/spencerskelly/Documents/Vaults/Model/Model/IPC !/03 Product Requirement/Engineering Requirements/MVS PRD/MVS PRD/2 Functional Requirements/2.5 Mechanical Requirements/2.5.4 Mean Time To Service.md
files.relativePath: Model/IPC !/03 Product Requirement/Engineering Requirements/MVS PRD/MVS PRD/2 Functional Requirements/2.5 Mechanical Requirements/2.5.4 Mean Time To Service.md
files.contentPreview: 2.5.4 Mean Time To Service The MTTS shall be five minutes when completed by trained facilities personnel. This shall be verified by timing all user serviceable part repairs and demonstrating compliance. The longest time to repair shall be less than ten minutes. EA Note eaGUID: {84CF979D-2787-4ccf-BC50-DC6EC0FB235E} Equivalent requirements for the PC25 are needed.

files.id: 9add6bfd3a35c8e4:Model/IPC !/03 Product Requirement/Engineering Requirements/MVS PRD/MVS PRD/2 Functional Requirements/2.5 Mechanical Requirements/2.5.5 Mean Time To Repair.md
files.absolutePath: /Users/spencerskelly/Documents/Vaults/Model/Model/IPC !/03 Product Requirement/Engineering Requirements/MVS PRD/MVS PRD/2 Functional Requirements/2.5 Mechanical Requirements/2.5.5 Mean Time To Repair.md
files.relativePath: Model/IPC !/03 Product Requirement/Engineering Requirements/MVS PRD/MVS PRD/2 Functional Requirements/2.5 Mechanical Requirements/2.5.5 Mean Time To Repair.md
files.contentPreview: 2.5.5 Mean Time To Repair The MTTR shall be one hour when completed by a trained field service technician or engineer. This shall be verified by identifying field repairable parts and demonstrating compliance. The Isolation Transformer contained in the MVS Server is excluded from this requirement. EA Note eaGUID: {84CF979D-2787-4ccf-BC50-DC6EC0FB235E} Equivalent requirements for the PC25 are needed.

files.absolutePath: /Users/spencerskelly/Documents/Vaults/Model/Model/IPC !/03 Product Requirement/Engineering Requirements/MVS PRD/MVS PRD/2 Functional Requirements/2.5 Mechanical Requirements/2.5.7 Mounting Requirement.md

files.contentPreview: 2.5.7 Mounting Requirement The MVS Server shall be floor mounted and shall be secured in four places. Mounting features shall not protrude beyond the cabinet outline.

files.id: 9add6bfd3a35c8e4:Model/IPC !/03 Product Requirement/Engineering Requirements/MVS PRD/MVS PRD/2 Functional Requirements/2.5 Mechanical Requirements/2.5.8 Surface Temperature.md
files.absolutePath: /Users/spencerskelly/Documents/Vaults/Model/Model/IPC !/03 Product Requirement/Engineering Requirements/MVS PRD/MVS PRD/2 Functional Requirements/2.5 Mechanical Requirements/2.5.8 Surface Temperature.md
files.relativePath: Model/IPC !/03 Product Requirement/Engineering Requirements/MVS PRD/MVS PRD/2 Functional Requirements/2.5 Mechanical Requirements/2.5.8 Surface Temperature.md
files.contentPreview:
2.5.8 Surface Temperature The MVS Server shall have the following maximum temperatures on exposed surfaces:
  • Handles or knobs that must be actuated at temperature: metallic, 50C. Non Metallic, 60C
  • A handle of knob that is contacted, but doesn’t involve lifting carrying or holding and other surfaces subject to contact in operation and user maintenance: Metallic: 60C. Non metallic 85C
  • A surface subject to casual contact: Metallic: 70C, Non metallic: 95C
EA Note eaGUID: {B4D73025-3562-4522-A53C-B7CE823D5EDE} Need equivalent requirements for the PCE25

files.id: 9add6bfd3a35c8e4:Model/IPC !/03 Product Requirement/Engineering Requirements/MVS PRD/MVS PRD/2 Functional Requirements/2.6 Environmental Requirements/2.6.1 Operating Temperature.md
files.absolutePath: /Users/spencerskelly/Documents/Vaults/Model/Model/IPC !/03 Product Requirement/Engineering Requirements/MVS PRD/MVS PRD/2 Functional Requirements/2.6 Environmental Requirements/2.6.1 Operating Temperature.md
files.relativePath: Model/IPC !/03 Product Requirement/Engineering Requirements/MVS PRD/MVS PRD/2 Functional Requirements/2.6 Environmental Requirements/2.6.1 Operating Temperature.md
files.contentPreview: 2.6.1 Operating Temperature The MVS Server shall be designed to operate from minus eighteen to forty five degrees Celsius at the rated load.

files.id: 9add6bfd3a35c8e4:Model/IPC !/03 Product Requirement/Engineering Requirements/MVS PRD/MVS PRD/2 Functional Requirements/2.6 Environmental Requirements/2.6.2 Operating Environment/2.6.2 Operating Environment.md

files.contentPreview: 2.6.2 Operating Environment The operating environment for the unit is an indoors industrial environment.

files.id: 9add6bfd3a35c8e4:Model/IPC !/03 Product Requirement/Engineering Requirements/MVS PRD/MVS PRD/2 Functional Requirements/2.6 Environmental Requirements/2.6.3 Storage Temperature.md
files.absolutePath: /Users/spencerskelly/Documents/Vaults/Model/Model/IPC !/03 Product Requirement/Engineering Requirements/MVS PRD/MVS PRD/2 Functional Requirements/2.6 Environmental Requirements/2.6.3 Storage Temperature.md
files.relativePath: Model/IPC !/03 Product Requirement/Engineering Requirements/MVS PRD/MVS PRD/2 Functional Requirements/2.6 Environmental Requirements/2.6.3 Storage Temperature.md
files.contentPreview: 2.6.3 Storage Temperature The MVS Server shall be designed to withstand a storage temperature of minus thirty six to sixty five degrees Celsius. No performance degradation shall occur after a one-month soak at either temperature extreme.

files.id: 9add6bfd3a35c8e4:Model/IPC !/03 Product Requirement/Engineering Requirements/MVS PRD/MVS PRD/2 Functional Requirements/2.6 Environmental Requirements/2.6.4 NEMA Rating.md

files.relativePath: Model/IPC !/03 Product Requirement/Engineering Requirements/MVS PRD/MVS PRD/2 Functional Requirements/2.6 Environmental Requirements/2.6.4 NEMA Rating.md
files.contentPreview: 2.6.4 NEMA Rating The enclosure shall be rated NEMA 2.

files.id: 9add6bfd3a35c8e4:Model/IPC !/03 Product Requirement/Engineering Requirements/MVS PRD/MVS PRD/2 Functional Requirements/2.6 Environmental Requirements/2.6.5 Corrosion Resistance.md

files.relativePath: Model/IPC !/03 Product Requirement/Engineering Requirements/MVS PRD/MVS PRD/2 Functional Requirements/2.6 Environmental Requirements/2.6.5 Corrosion Resistance.md
files.contentPreview: 2.6.5 Corrosion Resistance The MVS Server shall have corrosion resistance on all metal surfaces. The finish for corrosion resistance shall be Zinc Plate type II (gold) SC3 IAW ASTM B633.

files.id: 9add6bfd3a35c8e4:Model/IPC !/03 Product Requirement/Engineering Requirements/MVS PRD/MVS PRD/2 Functional Requirements/2.7 Interface Requirements/2.7.1 Status Indicators.md
files.absolutePath: /Users/spencerskelly/Documents/Vaults/Model/Model/IPC !/03 Product Requirement/Engineering Requirements/MVS PRD/MVS PRD/2 Functional Requirements/2.7 Interface Requirements/2.7.1 Status Indicators.md
files.relativePath: Model/IPC !/03 Product Requirement/Engineering Requirements/MVS PRD/MVS PRD/2 Functional Requirements/2.7 Interface Requirements/2.7.1 Status Indicators.md
files.contentPreview:
2.7.1 Status Indicators The MVS Server shall have the following status indicators:
  • An amber status indicator illuminated when power is applied to the unit.
  • A green status indicator when no faults are present in the unit and the DC Bus is ready.
  • A red status indicator that shows a thermal fault has occurred.

files.id: 9add6bfd3a35c8e4:Model/IPC !/03 Product Requirement/Engineering Requirements/MVS PRD/MVS PRD/2 Functional Requirements/2.7 Interface Requirements/2.7.2 Light Pole.md
files.absolutePath: /Users/spencerskelly/Documents/Vaults/Model/Model/IPC !/03 Product Requirement/Engineering Requirements/MVS PRD/MVS PRD/2 Functional Requirements/2.7 Interface Requirements/2.7.2 Light Pole.md
files.relativePath: Model/IPC !/03 Product Requirement/Engineering Requirements/MVS PRD/MVS PRD/2 Functional Requirements/2.7 Interface Requirements/2.7.2 Light Pole.md
files.contentPreview: 2.7.2 Light Pole A terminal block and mounting area shall be included and defined in the packaging for the product. The light pole shall have color definitions that match the status indicators specified.

files.id: 9add6bfd3a35c8e4:Model/IPC !/03 Product Requirement/Engineering Requirements/MVS PRD/MVS PRD/2 Functional Requirements/2.7 Interface Requirements/2.7.3 Power Disconnect.md
files.absolutePath: /Users/spencerskelly/Documents/Vaults/Model/Model/IPC !/03 Product Requirement/Engineering Requirements/MVS PRD/MVS PRD/2 Functional Requirements/2.7 Interface Requirements/2.7.3 Power Disconnect.md
files.relativePath: Model/IPC !/03 Product Requirement/Engineering Requirements/MVS PRD/MVS PRD/2 Functional Requirements/2.7 Interface Requirements/2.7.3 Power Disconnect.md
files.contentPreview: 2.7.3 Power Disconnect The MVS Server shall be designed to have a power disconnect circuit installed and shipped with the unit at the time of manufacture. The power disconnect shall be a mechanical configuration and shall remove power from all internal circuits. The power disconnect shall be an optional component.

files.id: 9add6bfd3a35c8e4:Model/IPC !/03 Product Requirement/Engineering Requirements/MVS PRD/MVS PRD/2 Functional Requirements/2.7 Interface Requirements/2.7.4 Control Interface Wiring.md
files.absolutePath: /Users/spencerskelly/Documents/Vaults/Model/Model/IPC !/03 Product Requirement/Engineering Requirements/MVS PRD/MVS PRD/2 Functional Requirements/2.7 Interface Requirements/2.7.4 Control Interface Wiring.md
files.relativePath: Model/IPC !/03 Product Requirement/Engineering Requirements/MVS PRD/MVS PRD/2 Functional Requirements/2.7 Interface Requirements/2.7.4 Control Interface Wiring.md
files.contentPreview: 2.7.4 Control Interface Wiring The MVS Server shall have a terminal block and wiring box consistent with UL and/or NEC requirements. In addition the wiring terminals shall be installed and maintained with standard electrician tools.

files.id: 9add6bfd3a35c8e4:Model/IPC !/03 Product Requirement/Engineering Requirements/MVS PRD/MVS PRD/2 Functional Requirements/2.7 Interface Requirements/2.7.5 Control Interface Function.md
files.absolutePath: /Users/spencerskelly/Documents/Vaults/Model/Model/IPC !/03 Product Requirement/Engineering Requirements/MVS PRD/MVS PRD/2 Functional Requirements/2.7 Interface Requirements/2.7.5 Control Interface Function.md
files.relativePath: Model/IPC !/03 Product Requirement/Engineering Requirements/MVS PRD/MVS PRD/2 Functional Requirements/2.7 Interface Requirements/2.7.5 Control Interface Function.md

hasPart: "[[Model/IPC !/03 Product Requirement/Engineering Requirements/MVS PRD/MVS PRD/2 Functional Requirements/2.7 Interface Requirements/2.7 Interface Requirements]]"

files.contentPreview: 2.7.5 Control Interface Function The MVS Server shall provide two terminals for control of the main contactor and two terminals for control of the pre-charge circuit. Both circuits shall be active when the terminals are shorted by contacts located in the master MVS Station.

files.id: 9add6bfd3a35c8e4:Model/IPC !/03 Product Requirement/Engineering Requirements/MVS PRD/MVS PRD/2 Functional Requirements/2.7 Interface Requirements/2.7.6 Control Interface Specification.md
files.absolutePath: /Users/spencerskelly/Documents/Vaults/Model/Model/IPC !/03 Product Requirement/Engineering Requirements/MVS PRD/MVS PRD/2 Functional Requirements/2.7 Interface Requirements/2.7.6 Control Interface Specification.md
files.relativePath: Model/IPC !/03 Product Requirement/Engineering Requirements/MVS PRD/MVS PRD/2 Functional Requirements/2.7 Interface Requirements/2.7.6 Control Interface Specification.md
files.contentPreview: 2.7.6 Control Interface Specification The open circuit voltage for the control interface shall be one hundred twenty volts AC nominal. The minimum current required to activate the control interface functions shall be less than fifty milli-amps. The maximum current allowed for the interface circuit shall be five amps. The master MVS Station shall be required to have contacts rated for a minimum of two hundred milli-amps and a maximum rating of five amps.

files.id: 9add6bfd3a35c8e4:Model/IPC !/03 Product Requirement/Engineering Requirements/MVS PRD/MVS PRD/2 Functional Requirements/2.7 Interface Requirements/2.7.7 Housekeeping Power.md
files.absolutePath: /Users/spencerskelly/Documents/Vaults/Model/Model/IPC !/03 Product Requirement/Engineering Requirements/MVS PRD/MVS PRD/2 Functional Requirements/2.7 Interface Requirements/2.7.7 Housekeeping Power.md
files.relativePath: Model/IPC !/03 Product Requirement/Engineering Requirements/MVS PRD/MVS PRD/2 Functional Requirements/2.7 Interface Requirements/2.7.7 Housekeeping Power.md
files.contentPreview: 2.7.7 Housekeeping Power The MVS Server shall provide one hundred twenty volts AC nominal at a power rating of twelve hundred watts. This power source shall be capable of sustaining a short in the wiring conduit and shall not damage the MVS Server. Replacement of a fusing device is acceptable.

files.id: 9add6bfd3a35c8e4:Model/IPC !/03 Product Requirement/Engineering Requirements/MVS PRD/MVS PRD/2 Functional Requirements/2.8 Service And Installation Requirements/2.8.1 Wiring Diagram.md
files.absolutePath: /Users/spencerskelly/Documents/Vaults/Model/Model/IPC !/03 Product Requirement/Engineering Requirements/MVS PRD/MVS PRD/2 Functional Requirements/2.8 Service And Installation Requirements/2.8.1 Wiring Diagram.md
files.relativePath: Model/IPC !/03 Product Requirement/Engineering Requirements/MVS PRD/MVS PRD/2 Functional Requirements/2.8 Service And Installation Requirements/2.8.1 Wiring Diagram.md
files.contentPreview: 2.8.1 Wiring Diagram The MVS Server shall contain a wiring diagram on the interior side of the removable front cover for the MVS Server. The wiring diagram shall include all replaceable components graphically represented. The wiring diagram shall have all major components graphically illustrated. The diagram shall be suitable for basic trouble-shooting activity.

files.id: 9add6bfd3a35c8e4:Model/IPC !/03 Product Requirement/Engineering Requirements/MVS PRD/MVS PRD/2 Functional Requirements/2.8 Service And Installation Requirements/2.8.2 Field Replaceable Components.md
files.absolutePath: /Users/spencerskelly/Documents/Vaults/Model/Model/IPC !/03 Product Requirement/Engineering Requirements/MVS PRD/MVS PRD/2 Functional Requirements/2.8 Service And Installation Requirements/2.8.2 Field Replaceable Components.md
files.relativePath: Model/IPC !/03 Product Requirement/Engineering Requirements/MVS PRD/MVS PRD/2 Functional Requirements/2.8 Service And Installation Requirements/2.8.2 Field Replaceable Components.md
files.contentPreview: 2.8.2 Field Replaceable Components All field replaceable components shall be accessible from the front or top of the MVS Server.

files.id: 9add6bfd3a35c8e4:Model/IPC !/03 Product Requirement/Engineering Requirements/MVS PRD/MVS PRD/2 Functional Requirements/2.8 Service And Installation Requirements/2.8.3 Voltage Taps Access.md
files.absolutePath: /Users/spencerskelly/Documents/Vaults/Model/Model/IPC !/03 Product Requirement/Engineering Requirements/MVS PRD/MVS PRD/2 Functional Requirements/2.8 Service And Installation Requirements/2.8.3 Voltage Taps Access.md
files.relativePath: Model/IPC !/03 Product Requirement/Engineering Requirements/MVS PRD/MVS PRD/2 Functional Requirements/2.8 Service And Installation Requirements/2.8.3 Voltage Taps Access.md
files.contentPreview: 2.8.3 Voltage Taps Access The voltage taps on the Power Isolation Transformer shall be configurable from the front or top of the MVS Server. Maximum service time for adjusting voltage taps shall be limited to twenty minutes by a trained field service technician.

files.id: 9add6bfd3a35c8e4:Model/IPC !/03 Product Requirement/Engineering Requirements/MVS PRD/MVS PRD/2 Functional Requirements/2.8 Service And Installation Requirements/2.8.4 Nominal Voltage Taps.md
files.absolutePath: /Users/spencerskelly/Documents/Vaults/Model/Model/IPC !/03 Product Requirement/Engineering Requirements/MVS PRD/MVS PRD/2 Functional Requirements/2.8 Service And Installation Requirements/2.8.4 Nominal Voltage Taps.md
files.relativePath: Model/IPC !/03 Product Requirement/Engineering Requirements/MVS PRD/MVS PRD/2 Functional Requirements/2.8 Service And Installation Requirements/2.8.4 Nominal Voltage Taps.md
files.contentPreview: 2.8.4 Nominal Voltage Taps The taps on the main transformer shall include the adjustable voltage taps for four hundred eighty volts and six hundred volts – line to line. The taps on the main transformer shall also include taps for changing the main transformer voltage by five percent positive or negative.

2.8.5 Additional Access Requirements
  • The MVS Server shall have a maximum of eight screws or bolts that must be removed for any service operation.
  • The MVS Server shall have a maximum of three screws to replace serviceable items like light bulbs or fuses.
  • The MVS Server shall have no special crimp tools required for installation or service. No special access limiting screws shall be used in this design.

03: Environmental
  • Operating Temperature: -25 to +75 degrees Celsius
  • Storage Temperature: -40 to +85 degrees Celsius
  • No Performance degradation shall occur after one-month soak at either temperature extreme at either extreme of the operating temperature.
  • Universal BMID shall operate in an industrial environment including battery acid, hydrogen gas.z

files.contentPreview: 2.3.3 Support Webasto Universal BMID Protocol (E43, E44) The Universal BMID shall support an application interface protocol to be supplied by Webasto. The Universal BMID will act as a server and respond to commands initiated from a client. Webasto will provide a means of testing this functionality during development. The protocol will support the following groups of messages. Measurement Data (E44) The following live measurement values shall be provided via the protocol at any time:  Pack Voltage  Mid-pack voltage  Battery Temperature (degrees Celsius)  Battery Current  Water level OK

2.5.3 System Wiring Interfaces (E54, E55, E56, E58)
  • 2 wires for Pack Voltage/Power Input (up to 110V); 36” 18 AWG 600V wire with ring terminal 22-16AWG, #6 insulated. (red = positive, black = negative)

  • 8 colored wires 18 AWG, 600V with these signals:
1. Water level sensor input (<3V = water low, 3-100V = water OK) (Gray) 2. Mid-pack voltage input (9-60VDC range) (Orange) 3. CAN-H (CAN signals defined in sec 2.3.3.4) (Yellow) 4. CAN-L (Green) 5. files.contentPreview: GSED1-Overview and Context This project defines the product and market requirements required to modernize the GSE charger display interface and enable High Voltage Power Station (HVPS) integration through targeted updates to the existing Gen 3 control architecture. Originally, GSE display modernization and HVPS communication were expected to be delivered through the broader �Gen 4 / Platform Comms (PCOM)� initiative, which included a new MK3 + adapter board architecture intended to introduce native communications (cellular, Wi-Fi, Ethernet), expanded processing capability, and a modernized display interface across both GSE and MHE portfolios. Due to cost constraints and architectural complexity, the PCOM initiative was narrowed and ultimately split. The MHE portfolio proceeded with a dedicated communications-focused redesign. The GSE portfolio is now being addressed independently with a more narrow scope.

files.id: 9add6bfd3a35c8e4:Model/IPC !/03 Product Requirement/Market Requirements/GSE Display/GSE Display MRD/GSED1-Overview and Context/GSED1.1-Scope of Work.md
files.absolutePath: /Users/spencerskelly/Documents/Vaults/Model/Model/IPC !/03 Product Requirement/Market Requirements/GSE Display/GSE Display MRD/GSED1-Overview and Context/GSED1.1-Scope of Work.md
files.relativePath: Model/IPC !/03 Product Requirement/Market Requirements/GSE Display/GSE Display MRD/GSED1-Overview and Context/GSED1.1-Scope of Work.md
files.contentPreview: GSED1.1-Scope of Work The current GSE scope is intentionally limited to: - Modernizing the GSE display interface to improve competitive positioning and technician usability - Updating the Gen 3 control board only as required to support HVPS communication and dynamic power allocation - Preserving the use of SkyLink kits as the primary mechanism for cloud telemetry and connectivity This effort is not a communications platform redesign. It's a targeted interface modernization and system-integration initiative.

files.absolutePath: /Users/spencerskelly/Documents/Vaults/Model/Model/IPC !/03 Product Requirement/Market Requirements/GSE Display/GSE Display MRD/GSED1-Overview and Context/GSED1.2-Core Objectives.md
files.relativePath: Model/IPC !/03 Product Requirement/Market Requirements/GSE Display/GSE Display MRD/GSED1-Overview and Context/GSED1.2-Core Objectives.md
files.contentPreview: GSED1.2-Core Objectives 1. Product Modernization Improve the visual presentation and perceived innovation of the GSE product line to address competitive pressure and support sales efforts. 2. Technician Usability Improvement Improve efficiency and intuitiveness of local configuration, diagnostics, and servicing workflows without expanding feature scope. 3. HVPS Communications Enablement Enable communication between our GSE chargers and the HVPS to allow dynamic power allocation and eliminate permanent system derating when HVPS is idle.

files.id: 9add6bfd3a35c8e4:Model/IPC !/03 Product Requirement/Market Requirements/GSE Display/GSE Display MRD/GSED1-Overview and Context/GSED1.3-Key Constraints and Dependencies.md

files.relativePath: Model/IPC !/03 Product Requirement/Market Requirements/GSE Display/GSE Display MRD/GSED1-Overview and Context/GSED1.3-Key Constraints and Dependencies.md
files.contentPreview: GSED1.3-Key Constraints and Dependencies Key constraints and assumptions include: - Native cellular, Wi-Fi, or Ethernet connectivity for GSE is out of scope. - SkyLink remains the primary cloud telemetry mechanism. - The updated design must preserve the reliability and durability standards associated with long-life GSE deployments. - Cost sensitivity is critical; architectural expansion beyond defined objectives must be avoided. - Modifications to the Gen 3 control board should be limited to what is necessary to achieve display modernization and HVPS communication enablement. The solution must align with existing enclosure, regulatory, and manufacturing constraints.

files.contentPreview: GSED2.02.prod-HMI Readability - Light A bright, color display is not trivial from a power and heat perspective. These chargers already operate in high-temperature ramp environments. If we increase display size and brightness without considering cabinet heat, we risk introducing reliability problems into a platform known for long service life. Modernization cannot come at the cost of long-term durability.

files.contentPreview: GSED2.02.sale-HMI Readability - Light Screen reflectiveness and longevity are major concerns. Is there potential for the control panel + buttons assembly able to be replaced without replacing the full door?

files.contentPreview: GSED2.16.prod-Backwards Compatibility and Retrofitting We have many existing units in the field. If this redesign requires a new enclosure cutout or full cabinet replacement, we lose the ability to offer upgrades to existing customers. That limits commercial upside and creates service friction. We need to preserve the option for customers to modernize existing deployments through a control board/HMI swap rather than a full system replacement.

files.contentPreview: GSED3.01.story-Simultaneous Dual-Port Status Visibility Today, the charger is physically dual-port, but the interface behaves like a single-port system. You must toggle between ports to see status or interact with settings. That creates friction. If this isn't corrected, the product continues to feel dated and unintuitive. A dual-port charger should behave like a dual-port system at first glance.

files.contentPreview: GSED3.08-Battery Information Visibility When a properly programmed PosiCharge BMID-equipped battery is connected, the HMI shall provide access to a Battery Information screen displaying available BMID-derived data, including: - Battery type / profile - Battery ID - Vehicle ID - BMID serial number - Battery voltage - Number of cells - Battery capacity - Equalization schedule status This information shall only be displayed when a battery is connected and properly identified.

headings: GSED4.01-Charger Control Board Programming via HMI
files.contentPreview: GSED4.01-Charger Control Board Programming via HMI The HMI shall enable local programming and configuration of charger control board parameters required for proper operation (Charger ID, Charger Serial Number, Max Port Current, kW Rating, Date and Time, etc.) without requiring external tools for standard setup tasks. This includes the ability to configure charger ID and operational parameters currently supported by the existing system.

headings: GSED4.01.prod-Charger Control Board Programming via HMI
files.contentPreview: GSED4.01.prod-Charger Control Board Programming via HMI Changing the charger configuration settings should still be locked by the key-code access sequence, but for someone who knows it, they should be able to change these settings using the HMI (i.e. we shouldn't require a laptop plug-in). Max port current and kW rating should be gated by a second, more complicated key code that we don't give out to just anyone (Level 2 permissions for dealer-level access). Customers should be able to touch anything currently under the charger configuration menu with the level 1 access code besides Max port current and kw rating.

headings: GSED4.01.story-Charger Control Board Programming via HMI
files.contentPreview: GSED4.01.story-Charger Control Board Programming via HMI Technicians rely on the charger display to program and identify units in the field. If charger ID or core control parameters require separate tools or external interfaces, setup becomes slower and more error-prone. The HMI must remain a primary configuration interface for the charger itself.

files.id: 9add6bfd3a35c8e4:Model/IPC !/03 Product Requirement/Market Requirements/Gen4 MRD/1 Overview/1.1 Objective.md
files.absolutePath: /Users/spencerskelly/Documents/Vaults/Model/Model/IPC !/03 Product Requirement/Market Requirements/Gen4 MRD/1 Overview/1.1 Objective.md
files.relativePath: Model/IPC !/03 Product Requirement/Market Requirements/Gen4 MRD/1 Overview/1.1 Objective.md

frontmatter.productManagementComment: This objective aligns with market demands for a more robust, streamlined, and cost-efficient solution, addressing growing fleet management challenges in the GSE and MHE industries.

files.contentPreview: 1.1 Objective The Gen IV Control/Comms Board aims to replace the current Raspberry Pi auxiliary Skylink kit system with a fully integrated and streamlined solution, enhancing reliability, ease of use, and scalability. This project will focus on improving diagnostic capabilities, connectivity, and configurability for maintenance technicians and fleet managers.

files.id: 9add6bfd3a35c8e4:Model/IPC !/03 Product Requirement/Market Requirements/Gen4 MRD/1 Overview/1.2 Scope.md
files.absolutePath: /Users/spencerskelly/Documents/Vaults/Model/Model/IPC !/03 Product Requirement/Market Requirements/Gen4 MRD/1 Overview/1.2 Scope.md
files.relativePath: Model/IPC !/03 Product Requirement/Market Requirements/Gen4 MRD/1 Overview/1.2 Scope.md
files.contentPreview: 1.2 Scope The Gen IV Control/Comms board will replace the existing Raspberry Pi Skylink kits by embedding communication, diagnostics, and control capabilities directly into the system. The system will support use cases for maintenance technicians, fleet managers, and operational teams, focusing on enhanced diagnostics, asset management, and real-time telemetry.

files.id: 9add6bfd3a35c8e4:Model/IPC !/03 Product Requirement/Market Requirements/Gen4 MRD/1 Overview/1.3 Context.md
files.absolutePath: /Users/spencerskelly/Documents/Vaults/Model/Model/IPC !/03 Product Requirement/Market Requirements/Gen4 MRD/1 Overview/1.3 Context.md
files.relativePath: Model/IPC !/03 Product Requirement/Market Requirements/Gen4 MRD/1 Overview/1.3 Context.md
files.contentPreview: 1.3 Context The current auxiliary Skylink kit system requires a Raspberry Pi mounted externally, leading to frequent reliability issues and increased field maintenance costs. Moving to an integrated solution resolves these challenges while reducing operational complexity.

files.id: 9add6bfd3a35c8e4:Model/IPC !/03 Product Requirement/Market Requirements/Gen4 MRD/1 Overview/1.4 Target Audience.md
files.absolutePath: /Users/spencerskelly/Documents/Vaults/Model/Model/IPC !/03 Product Requirement/Market Requirements/Gen4 MRD/1 Overview/1.4 Target Audience.md
files.relativePath: Model/IPC !/03 Product Requirement/Market Requirements/Gen4 MRD/1 Overview/1.4 Target Audience.md
files.contentPreview: 1.4 Target Audience The primary users of the Gen IV Control/Comms Board are: - Maintenance Technicians: On-site personnel conducting diagnostics and troubleshooting. - Fleet Managers: Remote users monitoring and managing multiple assets via software portals. (Asset Registration, Energy Reporting, Remote Access) - Energy/Utility Partners: Stakeholders requiring system-level energy management and reporting capabilities.

files.id: 9add6bfd3a35c8e4:Model/IPC !/03 Product Requirement/Market Requirements/Gen4 MRD/1 Overview/1.5 Key Feature Overview.md
files.absolutePath: /Users/spencerskelly/Documents/Vaults/Model/Model/IPC !/03 Product Requirement/Market Requirements/Gen4 MRD/1 Overview/1.5 Key Feature Overview.md
files.relativePath: Model/IPC !/03 Product Requirement/Market Requirements/Gen4 MRD/1 Overview/1.5 Key Feature Overview.md
files.contentPreview: 1.5 Key Feature Overview The Gen IV board shall enable the following key features: - Diagnostics: Enhanced on-site and remote fault analysis. - Connectivity: Support for Bluetooth, Wi-Fi, Ethernet, and cellular communication. - Asset Management: Simplified asset registration, authorization, and tracking - Energy Reporting: Full reporting for individual and bulk assets, Enable customers to track asset energy usage or bill for energy. - Configuration Tools: More intuitive interfaces for configuration.

files.id: 9add6bfd3a35c8e4:Model/IPC !/03 Product Requirement/Market Requirements/Gen4 MRD/1 Overview/1.6 Value Proposition.md
files.absolutePath: /Users/spencerskelly/Documents/Vaults/Model/Model/IPC !/03 Product Requirement/Market Requirements/Gen4 MRD/1 Overview/1.6 Value Proposition.md
files.relativePath: Model/IPC !/03 Product Requirement/Market Requirements/Gen4 MRD/1 Overview/1.6 Value Proposition.md
files.contentPreview: 1.6 Value Proposition The transition to an integrated Gen IV Control/Comms Board aligns with customer demand for reliability and scalability while addressing pain points associated with the current auxiliary Skylink kit. Value propositions include: - Improvde system reliability and reduced downtime. - Simplified hardware architecture, Streamline maintenance and reduce costs. - Enable full integration of diagnostics, configuration, and asset management into a single control system. - Reduce dependency on auxiliary hardware, increasing scalability.

files.contentPreview: 10 Network Connectivity & Configuration Configuring network connectivity for the Gen IV Control/Comms system must be designed to simplify and streamline the process compared to the current Skylink solution. The requirements must focus on making the system usable, secure, and efficient for installers and fleet managers, ensuring it meets market expectations for reliability and ease of deployment.

frontmatter.userStory: Installers want flexible options for network connectivity to ensure the system can be configured in any operational environment, even in locations with limited infrastructure. Cellular connectivity should include a sim that supports multiple carriers. Eac

headings: CC82 Support for Multiple Network Protocols
files.contentPreview: CC82 Support for Multiple Network Protocols The system shall support configuration for multiple network protocols, including: - Ethernet: Ensure active connection detection. - Wi-Fi: Allow input of SSID and password. - Cellular: Validate SIM card credentials and include multi-carrier SIM (domestic + international support) - Serial Port: Provide fallback for configuration in cases where other methods fail. - Bluetooth: Enable secure and quick setup during initial configuration.

frontmatter.userStory: Installers want a simplified interface to reduce the time and complexity of setting up network connectivity, minimizing errors and ensuring a positive installation experience.

files.contentPreview: CC83 Intuitive Network Configuration Process The system shall provide an intuitive interface for network configuration. Including: - Auto-detection of available network protocols and prioritization based on speed and reliability. - Real-time feedback for successful or failed connection attempts, with clear error messages (e.g., "Invalid credentials," "Network unavailable").

In addition, switching between network modes shall not result in critical data loss or significant system downtime.

files.contentPreview: CC85 Offline Operation and Configuration The system shall continue to function without network connectivity and store critical configuration locally. Offline configurations must automatically sync with the backend when connectivity is restored.

frontmatter.userStory: Maintenance teams  want diagnostics tools (on-site & remote) to quickly identify and resolve network issues, reducing service time and avoiding escalations to technical support.

headings: CC86 Diagnostics and Troubleshooting for Connectivity Issues
files.contentPreview: CC86 Diagnostics and Troubleshooting for Connectivity Issues The system shall provide tools to diagnose and troubleshoot connectivity issues, including: - Viewing communication logs for error patterns. - Running diagnostics tests for each network protocol. These options shall be available both for on-site diagnostics and remote troubleshooting.

frontmatter.productManagementComment: - Reporting Frequency: Set how often logged data is uploaded to the backend (e.g., real-time, hourly, daily, on event). *This is something we should set in our design, make sure it's not like the current Skylink reporting frequency.

files.contentPreview: CC109 Charger Parameter Configuration (Remote) The system shall allow fleet managers and authorized personnel to remotely view and modify non-critical, non-control parameters via the backend. These parameters shall include: - Charger Temperature Readout Settings (Celsius vs. Farenheit) -Charger Information (Charger ID, Port ID, Charger Name) - Daylight Savings Time Adjustments - Diagnostics Logging Parameters: -Set fault logging frequency (e.g., continuous, every X minutes, event-driven). - Configure parameters for system status reporting (e.g., operational state, error states). Event Notification Preferences: -Enable/Disable notifications for specific event types (e.g., fault occurrence, maintenance reminders). - Define thresholds for event notifications (e.g., temperature exceeds X degrees, energy usage exceeds Y kWh). - Select preferred notification methods (e.g., email, SMS, push notifications).

headings: CC01  Asset Registration via Charger Plug-In (Automatic Registration)
files.contentPreview: CC01 Asset Registration via Charger Plug-In (Automatic Registration) The system shall automatically register a vehicle as an asset when it plugs into a Gen IV charger for the first time and initiates a charging session. The registration process shall capture and associate the following data: - Vehicle ID - Battery ID - BMID Serial Number

frontmatter.productManagementComment: This is critical to ensuring data integrity. If a dealer/VAR/fleet manager is using the portal to register assets, then we must provide them with real-time feedback on whether their inputs are valid. By checking against our system database, we can prevent

files.contentPreview: CC05 Asset Registration - System Validation The system shall validate all inputs during asset registration to ensure: - Correct data format for Vehicle ID, Battery ID, and BMID Serial Number. - Absence of duplicate asset entries. - Identification of invalid or missing fields with real-time feedback. files.contentPreview: CC11 Authorization/Deauthorization of Assets The system shall allow installers or fleet managers to assign and modify the authorization status of vehicle assets within the cloud portal. If an asset is authorized, the chargers shall allow it to charge and log energy usage. If an asset is deauthorized, the chargers shall block it from charging and provide a notification to the user indicating the asset is unauthorized.

files.contentPreview: CC16 Display - Physical Appearance & Standards The system shall include a high-quality, easily readable display that is durable, user-friendly, and resistant to long-term environmental wear. The display shall meet the following design and functional guidelines: 1) Size & Readability: The display must be large enough to be easily readable at a glance, even from a reasonable working distance. frontmatter.userStory: Fleet managers and maintenance personnel need to be immediately notified of critical faults to minimize operational disruptions and ensure timely intervention.

files.contentPreview: CC64 Alerts & Notifications - Fault The system shall provide real-time fault notifications via email, SMS, and mobile app push notifications to designated recipients based on configurable alert settings.

files.id: 9add6bfd3a35c8e4:Model/IPC !/03 Product Requirement/Market Requirements/Gen4 MRD/6 Fault Monitoring - Remote/CC65 View Fault & Diagnostic Data - Remote.md
files.absolutePath: /Users/spencerskelly/Documents/Vaults/Model/Model/IPC !/03 Product Requirement/Market Requirements/Gen4 MRD/6 Fault Monitoring - Remote/CC65 View Fault & Diagnostic Data - Remote.md

files.basename: CC65 View Fault & Diagnostic Data - Remote

frontmatter.userStory: Fleet managers need to access detailed fault information to determine root causes and identify trends in recurring issues.

headings: CC65 View Fault & Diagnostic Data - Remote
files.contentPreview: CC65 View Fault & Diagnostic Data - Remote The system shall allow users to remotely review detailed fault diagnostics via the cloud portal, including: - Fault name & error codes - Fault timestamp - Diagnostics logs leading up to fault (Operational, External Device, Comms) - Fault location (charger ID, vehicle ID, port ID, site location)

files.id: 9add6bfd3a35c8e4:Model/IPC !/03 Product Requirement/Market Requirements/Gen4 MRD/6 Fault Monitoring - Remote/CC66 Remote Diagnostics - Operational Logs.md
files.absolutePath: /Users/spencerskelly/Documents/Vaults/Model/Model/IPC !/03 Product Requirement/Market Requirements/Gen4 MRD/6 Fault Monitoring - Remote/CC66 Remote Diagnostics - Operational Logs.md
files.relativePath: Model/IPC !/03 Product Requirement/Market Requirements/Gen4 MRD/6 Fault Monitoring - Remote/CC66 Remote Diagnostics - Operational Logs.md

frontmatter.userStory: Fleet managers want to remotely access operational logs to analyze the system's  performance and identify abnormal patterns or events leading to faults.

files.contentPreview: CC66 Remote Diagnostics - Operational Logs The system shall allow users to remotely view operational logs via the cloud portal, including: - Power Delivery Data (Input Voltage, Output Voltage, Current Levels) - Asset Information (Battery ID, Vehicle ID, Charger ID, BMID ID, Port ID) - Total Energy Usage Summary -Temperature Data (Thermistor Reporting) - Charging Session(s) Info: Session ID, Energy Usage (AC/DC), Session Duration, Session Start/End Times

files.id: 9add6bfd3a35c8e4:Model/IPC !/03 Product Requirement/Market Requirements/Gen4 MRD/6 Fault Monitoring - Remote/CC67 Remote Diagnostics - External Device Logs.md

files.relativePath: Model/IPC !/03 Product Requirement/Market Requirements/Gen4 MRD/6 Fault Monitoring - Remote/CC67 Remote Diagnostics - External Device Logs.md
files.basename: CC67 Remote Diagnostics - External Device Logs

frontmatter.priority: Should Have for comms w/ our own BMIDs\nCould Have otherwise
frontmatter.productManagementComment: External devices (vehicles + non-Posicharge BMIDs) may have security protocols that disallow us from pulling information from them. We should be able to view logs and communciate with our own systems, but may not be able to for external systems depending
frontmatter.userStory: Fleet managers want  to remotely view external device communication logs to ensure proper data transmission between the charger and external devices (BMID or vehicles) and identify any potential interface issues.

headings: CC67 Remote Diagnostics - External Device Logs
files.contentPreview: CC67 Remote Diagnostics - External Device Logs The system shall allow users to remotely view logs for connected external devices via a cloud portal, including: - BMID communication logs (e.g., connection type, signal strength, transmission errors). - Vehicle logs (e.g., vehicle ID, fault codes generated by connected equipment).

files.id: 9add6bfd3a35c8e4:Model/IPC !/03 Product Requirement/Market Requirements/Gen4 MRD/6 Fault Monitoring - Remote/CC68 Remote Diagnostics - Communications Logs.md
files.absolutePath: /Users/spencerskelly/Documents/Vaults/Model/Model/IPC !/03 Product Requirement/Market Requirements/Gen4 MRD/6 Fault Monitoring - Remote/CC68 Remote Diagnostics - Communications Logs.md
files.relativePath: Model/IPC !/03 Product Requirement/Market Requirements/Gen4 MRD/6 Fault Monitoring - Remote/CC68 Remote Diagnostics - Communications Logs.md

frontmatter.userStory: Fleet managers want to remotely view communication failures by reviewing historical logs of communication protocols and identifying packet transmission issues to determine if faults are related to connectivity.
frontmatter.productManagementComment: One of the biggest problems we have in the field is unreliable connectivity, leading to significant amounts of customer data being lost. We need to have a system to understand what causes our systems to go offline so we can effectively troubleshoot these

files.contentPreview: CC68 Remote Diagnostics - Communications Logs The system shall allow users to remotely view communication logs via the cloud portal, including: - System-level communication protocols (e.g., CAN bus activity, OCPP/MQTT logs). - Error codes related to failed data packets (sent/received). - Communications with external devices (BMID, Vehicle)

files.id: 9add6bfd3a35c8e4:Model/IPC !/03 Product Requirement/Market Requirements/Gen4 MRD/6 Fault Monitoring - Remote/CC69 Remote Diagnostics - Filter - Sort Log Data.md

files.basename: CC69 Remote Diagnostics - Filter - Sort Log Data

frontmatter.userStory: Fleet managers  want to remotely isolate and analyze specific log entries without navigating excessive data, enabling them to focus on relevant diagnostics quickly.

headings: CC69 Remote Diagnostics - Filter/Sort Log Data
files.contentPreview: CC69 Remote Diagnostics - Filter/Sort Log Data The system shall allow maintenance technicians to filter and sort retrieved log data based on parameters such as: - Date/time range. - Fault severity (critical, warning, informational). - Site/Location -Client/Airline -Asset Type -Unique Identifiers (Serial #, Charger ID, Battery ID, Vehicle ID)

files.id: 9add6bfd3a35c8e4:Model/IPC !/03 Product Requirement/Market Requirements/Gen4 MRD/6 Fault Monitoring - Remote/CC70 Assign Faults for Resolution.md
files.absolutePath: /Users/spencerskelly/Documents/Vaults/Model/Model/IPC !/03 Product Requirement/Market Requirements/Gen4 MRD/6 Fault Monitoring - Remote/CC70 Assign Faults for Resolution.md
files.relativePath: Model/IPC !/03 Product Requirement/Market Requirements/Gen4 MRD/6 Fault Monitoring - Remote/CC70 Assign Faults for Resolution.md

frontmatter.userStory: Fleet managers want to delegate fault resolution efficiently and track assigned maintenance tasks to ensure accountability and timely repair.
frontmatter.salesComment: Can we have a ticket pop up when you click on a fault? That way, a customer can easily submit a ticket to us or our VAR for service with details on the fault

files.contentPreview: CC70 Assign Faults for Resolution The system shall allow authorized users to assign detected faults to specific maintenance teams, track resolution progress, and log comments or status updates.

frontmatter.productManagementComment: \"Report\" is a relative term. Any formatting we can do to make it easier for our field service / maintenance teams to navigate is helpful, but bare minimum we need to be able to export some sort of CSV/Excel of this information.
frontmatter.userStory: Fleet managers need to document fault occurrences and resolutions for regulatory compliance, reporting, and data analysis.

headings: CC71 System - Automated Fault Report Generation (Remote)
files.contentPreview: CC71 System - Automated Fault Report Generation (Remote) The system shall automatically generate a pre-filled fault report containing: - Fault ID, Fault name/description, type, and timestamp. - Fault set date/time, Fault clear date/time - Charger State (e.g., Equalizing, Recovery Charging). - Fault Severity (e.g., Critical, Warning). - Asset details (Vehicle ID, Battery ID, Charger ID, BMID Serial Number). - Software version, Hardware Revision, and Generation (e.g., Gen II, Gen III).

headings: CC72 Request External Service for Fault Resolution
files.contentPreview: CC72 Request External Service for Fault Resolution The system shall allow fleet managers to escalate fault resolution by requesting service from: - IT Teams - Internal Maintenance - Installer/Dealer -Manufacturer Support

frontmatter.userStory: Fleet managers want chargers to be compatible with third-party energy management and vehicle fleet platforms using OCPP, so they can be integrated into their existing charging ecosystem without vendor lock-in.
frontmatter.productManagementComment: 1) OCPP (Open Charge Point Protocol) is the most widely used protocol for managing EV chargers remotely, allowing communication with third-party backend systems.\n2) Many airport and  fleet operators require OCPP support to integrate with their energy man

headings: CC73 Support for OCPP (Open Charge Point Protocol)
files.contentPreview: CC73 Support for OCPP (Open Charge Point Protocol) The system shall support OCPP (1.6 & 2.0.1) to enable standardized communication between the charger and third-party backend systems, facilitating universal compatibility with non-Posicharge infrastructure.

frontmatter.productManagementComment: 1)  ISO 15118 enables Plug & Charge, allowing vehicles to authenticate automatically when plugged into a charger.\n2) This standard is increasingly adopted for both industrial and on-road EVs.\n3) ISO 15118 allows future support of bidirectional charging
frontmatter.userStory: Fleet managers want their chargers to automatically recognize and authenticate vehicles via plug & charge, ensuring a secure, easy charging experience.

headings: CC74 Support for ISO 15118 (Plug & Charge & V2G)
files.contentPreview: CC74 Support for ISO 15118 (Plug & Charge & V2G) The system shall support ISO 15118, enabling vehicle-to-charger communication for authentication, we well as the potential for future bidirectional energy transfer (V2G - Vehicle-to-Grid).

frontmatter.productManagementComment: 1) CAN Bus is a standard communication method with many industrial vehicles.\n2) As high throughput operations expand their fleet to include more vehicles with lithium batteries, we'll need CAN communication to ensure we can charge these batteries and rem

files.contentPreview: CC75 Support for CAN Communication The system shall support CAN Bus protocols to ensure direct communication with industrial vehicles and lithium battery management systems (BMS), enabling better data exchange and real-time diagnostics. - We should aim to integrate all capabilities of the auxiliary G-Can board kit into the system natively.

frontmatter.productManagementComment: In competitive bids where a customer already has an existing charging infrastructure, Bluetooth communication positions our system as a flexible, universal alternative that can replace existing solutions without requiring extensive vehicle modifications.

files.contentPreview: CC76 Support for Bluetooth Communication The system shall support Bluetooth communication to enable connectivity with both: 1) A mobile application for diagnostics, configuration, data collection, and monitoring. 2) A wireless BMID to facilitate charger-to-BMID communication without requiring a wired connection.

files.basename: CC77 Remote Over the Air (OTA) Updates for Firmware & Software

frontmatter.productManagementComment: 1) Firmware updates should be delivered remotely, ensuring that chargers always run on the latest approved, secure software.\n2) OTA updates must include rollback capabilities, ensuring chargers revert to the lsat known working version if an update fails.
frontmatter.userStory: Posicharge needs the ability to push firmware and software updates to all chargers remotely so that we can quickly deploy fixes and enhancements without requiring on-site intervention.

headings: CC77 Remote Over the Air (OTA) Updates for Firmware & Software
files.contentPreview: CC77 Remote Over the Air (OTA) Updates for Firmware & Software The system shall support secure Over-the-Air (OTA) updates for all firmware and software components, enabling remote deployment of patches, feature upgrades, and security fixes across all connected chargers. - Chargers operating offline should support scheduled update syncing when connectivity is restored.

files.relativePath: Model/IPC !/03 Product Requirement/Market Requirements/Gen4 MRD/8 OTA Capabilities/CC78 Software Versioning & Rollback Capabilities.md

frontmatter.userStory: Posicharge wants a robust versioning system so that updates can be applied or rolled back without risking charger downtime or bricking hardware.
frontmatter.productManagementComment: 1) Firmware version tracking ensures devices always run the latest stable release.\n2) If an update fails, the system should automatically revert to the last working version to prevent bricked devices.

files.contentPreview: CC78 Software Versioning & Rollback Capabilities The system shall support version-controlled firmware updates with an option to rollback to previous stable versions if a failure occurs.

files.contentPreview: CC80 Data Access - Local Tools The system shall allow authorized partners to decrypt data through the use of Posicharge local desktop tools/programs, such as the ChargerTools SW.

files.contentPreview: Operational Independence of Control and Comms The system shall ensure operational independence between the control and comms functions. Communications, telemetry, load management, and OTA functionality shall not compromise or starve real-time charging control processes. This includes: - Guaranteed execution priority for safety-critical control loops - Isolation between comms workloads and charging control - Protection against OTA, logging, or load-management tasks blocking charging behavior In the event of a comms failure, the charger shall continue to operate without disruption. Loss of connectivity must not disable charging capability. Recovery of comms shall avoid charger downtime where feasible. Operational Independence of Control and Comms - Product eaGUID: {FA321CC7-7230-4d63-A196-546124B837BC} It would be good to have a fault or some indication specifying when comms are down. This way, we can know when there's a comms issue vs. a full issue with the charger Operational Independe

files.contentPreview: Processing, Memory, and Headroom The system shall be architected with sufficient processing performance, memory, and storage headroom to support current connectivity, telemetry, OTA, battery profiles, and load-management requirements, while preserving capacity for future expansion without requiring a board redesign. This includes headroom for: - Event-driven telemetry architecture - Secure OTA with rollback and buffering - Local load-management execution - Local log storage and buffering - Unified Portal integrations - Lead Acid Battery Profiles - Expanding Lithium Battery Integrations Processing, Memory, and Headroom - Product eaGUID: {E1D39CD8-FDB0-4efd-BB1D-2C53A0DD206E} We originally prioritized MHE Comms due to the ProCore Edge memory constraints, thus limiting our ability to further expand lithium integrations. We need to ensure there's enough memory/data handling capacity in the architecture to support all identified functions.

headings: Log and Diagnostic File Syncing  - User Story
files.contentPreview: Log and Diagnostic File Syncing The system shall support deferred and conditional upload of logs and diagnostic files, including: - Fault/Warning (Diagnostic) logs - Charge Event Log - Charger Daily Performance Log - Charger History Log This shall include the ability to: - Upload logs automatically when a fault occurs - Upload logs on a scheduled interval (every two hours, daily) - Upload logs only when requested by the backend or service teams Log and Diagnostic File Syncing - User Story eaGUID: {922259D0-1889-4233-A016-E08C0E32B89B} The goal is to minimize data usage and hardware strain while ensuring service teams can retrieve diagnostics when needed.

files.contentPreview: OCPP Enablement The system shall support OCPP (minimum 1.6) to enable: - Charger to backend communication - Charger-to-third party management and energy platforms - Participation in site-level and enterprise-level energy/load demand management systems - Interoperability alongside EVSE and DCFC This enables standardized communication between the charger and third-party backend systems, facilitating universal compatibility with non-Posicharge infrastructure. OCPP shall be supported over the system's primary backhaul connectivity interfaces (Ethernet, WiFi, Cellular). OCPP Enablement - User Story eaGUID: {6B72AB4E-B957-4965-833D-FFEF71A4A95E} Enterprise customers want chargers to integrate into existing third party ecosystems/management systems without vendor lock-in. OCPP enables communication with external systems (i.e. EVSE chargers and DC Fast chargers).

headings: OTA - Bandwidth and Data Plan Awareness
OTA - Bandwidth and Data Plan Awareness - User Story
files.contentPreview: OTA - Bandwidth and Data Plan Awareness The system of OTA mechanisms shall support strategies that minimize data consumption, including: -Staggered/Sequenced update scheduling - Off-peak update execution - Conditional downloads OTA - Bandwidth and Data Plan Awareness - User Story eaGUID: {571B94C0-64A4-42ce-8B3E-0D6ABEAD4C90} The goal is to ensure that OTA does not destroy the commercial viability of cellular deployments.

headings: OTA - Centralized Control and Authorization - User Story
files.contentPreview: OTA - Centralized Control and Authorization OTA update initiation shall be centrally controlled by Ampure/PosiCharge. The system shall enable: - Restriction of OTA execution to authorized PosiCharge service, ENG, or OPS roles - A controlled mechanism for customers to request updates (not initiate them freely) -Enforcement of permissions that prevent unrestricted customer-initiated OTA activity OTA - Centralized Control and Authorization - User Story eaGUID: {389D8208-AB42-445e-832A-4C5AFE6DA8F3} The goal is to prevent unsafe update behavior, protect hardware integrity, and control bandwidth usage.

files.basename: OTA - Offline and Intermittent Connectivity Handling
headings: OTA - Offline and Intermittent Connectivity Handling
OTA - Offline and Intermittent Connectivity Handling - User Story
files.contentPreview: OTA - Offline and Intermittent Connectivity Handling The system shall support: - Queuing of updates when devices are offline - Resumption of interrupted updates - Safe deferral if connectivity degrades - Automatic retry policies OTA - Offline and Intermittent Connectivity Handling - User Story eaGUID: {A8106CCE-A429-43ee-B592-F5EDFBCBB13F} Most deployments are in industrial environments where connectivity may be weak, not always available, or unstable/intermittent. OTA must be capable of working even in these sub-optimal conditions.

files.id: 9add6bfd3a35c8e4:Model/IPC !/03 Product Requirement/Market Requirements/MHE Comms Controller/MHE Comms Controller/Connectivity, Interoperability, and Local Interaction/OTA - Scalability and Deployment/OTA - Scalability and Deployment.md

headings: OTA - Scalability and Deployment - User Story
files.contentPreview: OTA - Scalability and Deployment The system shall be capable of supporting OTA deployment at fleet scale, including: - Individual device updates - Group or site-level updates OTA infrastructure shall support: -Staged rollouts - Pausing or halting deployments -Targeted updates to specific charger populations Grouping for rollout eaGUID: {6405227F-7046-49b6-AC2B-1731DD8E8E38} How would we want this group selected? by site? by SN like last two digits? By user controlled groups? Usage priority? Customer can turn off auto-OTA? OTA - Scalability and Deployment - Product eaGUID: {15C4EA9A-42A2-4a92-8599-C5A695A200D9} Need sales feedback: In what time window should a critical patch reasonably be deployable (hours, days, weeks)? OTA - Scalability and Deployment - User Story eaGUID: {1DF07FE8-04EF-4a8b-9C7C-2724232AC3DA} The goal is to ensure OTA can support major operational rollouts (large fleets), not just controlled, individual lab updates.

headings: OTA - Software Versioning & Rollback Capabilities - User Story
OTA - Software Versioning & Rollback Capabilities - Engineering
files.contentPreview: OTA - Software Versioning & Rollback Capabilities The system shall support version-controlled firmware updates with an option to rollback to previous stable versions if a failure occurs. The system shall support: - Verification of update integrity before installation - Monitoring of update status (queued, in progress, completed, failed) - Automatic failure detection - Rollback to last-known-good versions - Prevention of device bricking The system shall enable visibility into: - Which devices are on which versions -Devices requiring recovery action Internal View eaGUID: {F576DDFF-320C-43e6-83A1-C4C434B821E1} Sort and filter assets by firmware or other configuration See if units have not updated but are connected OTA - Software Versioning & Rollback Capabilities - User Story eaGUID: {C3F5B650-0857-493d-811D-CA89511439FE} Posicharge wants a robust versioning system so that updates can be applied or rolled back without risking charger downtime or bricking hardware. headings: Fail-Safe and Reduced Operation - Load Management
files.contentPreview: Fail-Safe and Reduced Operation - Load Management The system shall define and support safe degraded operating modes for load management. This includes the ability to: - Default chargers to conservative power limits if coordination signals are lost - Preserve last-known-safe power caps during communication outages - Prevent uncontrolled full-power operation when cloud-based load coordination is unavailable - Recover without requiring full manual reconfiguration

headings: Load Management Control Architecture - User Story
files.contentPreview: Load Management Control Architecture The system shall support both centralized (backend-driven) and localized (site-level) load management control architectures. This includes preserving the ability for: - Charger behavior to be influenced by backend systems (PosiCharge or third-party) - Charger behavior to respond to locally available site signals (e.g., meters, site controllers) - Site-level coordination without requiring continuous high-availability cloud connectivity The system shall not assume that all power management intelligence resides only in the cloud. Load Management Control Architecture - Product eaGUID: {AAF9D962-96B2-4aa4-A680-8F6CCF864926} Are there any specific requirements about whether load management must be wired or wireless? If it's WiFi, the facility needs to have a Wifi router we can connect to. If it's cellular, then it would be controlled via cloud. If it's Ethernet, there would need to be a LAN connection. This impacts how the full system would be configured.

headings: Priority and Rule-Based Charging - User Story
files.contentPreview: Priority and Rule-Based Charging The system shall preserve the ability to incorporate vehicle or battery state of charge into power allocation decisions. This includes enabling capabilities such as: - Prioritizing based on vehicle type - Prioritizing based on SOC - Operational schedules and readiness rules - IConditional power policies applied to charger groups. The system shall not constrain responsiveness to only static power caps. Priority and Rule-Based Charging - User Story eaGUID: {1A03A951-BECE-4c2c-841B-84229A3E0C17} Operators want critical forklifts/vehicles/batteries charged first. . Operators may want to set an SOC threshold (i.e. prioritize getting all vehicles to 50% SOC). Operators may also want the ability to prioritize certain vehicle types (i.e. heavy duty vehicles). The goal is to allow customers to intentionally operate fleets, not just restrict them.

headings: Utility/Facility Load Signal Responsiveness - User Story
files.contentPreview: Utility/Facility Load Signal Responsiveness The system shall preserve the ability to respond to external load reduction signals and react to meter data within timeframes that are operationally meaningful (minutes, not hours), without assuming sub-second real-time control. Utility/Facility Load Signal Responsiveness - User Story eaGUID: {09950A4D-BB52-4c18-940C-6641047DC337} The goal is to support real demand-charge management and time of use strategies without forcing unnecessary real-time control complexity.

Additionally, it can provide battery-charging parameters to a Bluetooth enabled charger. 1.2 Abbreviations / Definitions: BLE - Bluetooth Low Energy BMID - Battery Monitor Identification Device CAN - Controller Area Network CE - Conformité Européenne certification CSA - Canadian Standard CUL - conforms to CSA standards by UL EQ - Equalization Charge IFETEL - The Federal Telecommunications Institute LED - Light Emitting Diode LE-SPS - Low Energy Serial Port Service LoRa - Long Range Communication LoRaWAN - Network Protocol for LoRa communication Mk III Board – Webasto communication board developed for the Mark III wall box MTBF - Mean Time Between Failures MTTR - Mean

files.contentPreview: E35: Charging State Data Following charging state parameters shall be stored in non-volatile memory of the BMID. They will be updated by BMID and can also be overridden when sent from a Bluetooth/LORA client. These parameters must also be readable from a Bluetooth/LORA client at any time. Below parameters can be sent from any Bluetooth/LORA client and the last saved values of these items can also be read back by a Bluetooth/LORA client at any time Battery SOC BMID shall update based on positive or negative current draw Value sent via Bluetooth will reset to new start point. EQ minute count (An EQ is completed when the EQ minute count reaches the Minimum EQ minutes in the Battery Configuration) Accumulate during EQ charging (Current below Max Finish Current plus a margin when SOC is close to 100%) Reset on entry to a new EQ window If not using EQ window, reset when reaching max days or max amp-hours since last completed EQ (from Battery Configuration) Amp-hours since last EQ Accumulate

files.contentPreview: 1.0 Overview The ProCore Edge enclosure redesign is a strategic cost-down and platform ownership initiative, not a cosmetic redesign. Today, PosiCharge purchases fully assembled ProCore Edge cabinets from Delta Electronics. While Delta-s power modules are cost-effective on a $/kW basis, the cabinet and mechanical system are over-engineered, expensive, and are the primary driver of low contribution margin across the ProCore Edge line. In parallel, Ampure acquired Power Designers (Florida), which designs and manufactures its own industrial charger enclosures. Power Designers consistently outperforms Ampure on contribution margin despite using more expensive power modules, largely due to low-cost, internally owned cabinet designs and localized manufacturing. The goal of this project is to: - Establish a PosiCharge-owned ProCore Edge enclosure platform - Shift cabinet manufacturing from Delta Electronics to Power Designers (FL) - Continue sourcing Delta power modules only - Materially impr

(See Sales Comment) Cabinet COGS Reduction - Product eaGUID: {D4F992B0-8B91-4193-81CC-BB88311DC9AD} How much price flexibility/CM improvement would improve competitiveness? Cost per kW for PD is $186 (~75% higher than PCE). We have ~21% margin on our 5B, 15 kW cabinet. In a 10B cabinet at 18 kW, CM goes down to 7%. PD CM for a 15 kW is ~30% at a lower price point. PCE cabinet cost before tariffs is $2274 (+25% with tariffs). With 2274 as a ceiling, subtracting -$337 ($1937). files.contentPreview: Regions for Sales The system shall be sellable in the US, MX, and Europe. Selling in Canada is questionable (see sales comment). Regions for Sales - Product eaGUID: {D77290AA-2D5F-4006-B848-C406E435178E} What markets do we need to be capable of selling into besides the US? Keep in mind that since we're touching the controller, we'll need a full system re-certification for each region. Regions for Sales - Sales eaGUID: {7B68BFB6-D6ED-40af-A741-FFA0C7B0A728} Selling in Canada is dependent on how much we'd need to overbuild the 480 VAC cabinet to meet the 600VAC requirements. 600 VAC cabinets need more space than 480 VAC to meet the regulatory cubic inch requirements.

headings: External Sequencer Interface Support - User Story
files.contentPreview: External Sequencer Interface Support The cabinet platform shall support the ability to interface with an external sequencing or load-sharing device (e.g., PD-DUO--type systems) that enables a single charger or stacked system to serve two vehicles either sequentially or concurrently. External Sequencer Interface Support - User Story eaGUID: {1F09EDC8-3BFB-4df0-8AF2-65CE26961BB3} We want the cabinet to be architected such that future shared-charger or sequencer solutions can be supported without a cabinet redesign, enabling multi-vehicle charging use cases that are increasingly relevant for lithium fleets. External Sequencer Interface Support - Sales eaGUID: {DD17B31C-C192-4d97-95E7-D11CA27AFBD3} This is a nice to have feature. If there's a minor cost impact, it would be nice to preserve compatibility for a sequencer accessory, but it's not a hard requirement.

headings: Modular Output Cable Interface - User Story
files.contentPreview: Modular Output Cable Interface The cabinet platform shall support a modular output interface that allows DC cables to be configured, tested, and shipped independently of the charger. Modular Output Cable Interface - Product eaGUID: {5856FAD2-C42C-4197-AD36-05DD8A4BCC00} This was brought up by Blake as something that Enatel does on their chargers. Enatel does this with an SB350 and a separate comm connection. Max output per cabinet is 350A. While this may add cost to the cabinet, it would result in EOL and labor savings in the manufacturing process. Modular Output Cable Interface - Sales eaGUID: {3C651A58-999E-48e9-B6FA-0BBD8E6AFD74} We'd like this implemented, but there's a dependency on cost. Depending on how expensive this implementation is, we may choose to deviate. Modularity - User Story eaGUID: {633CC08A-7E8F-4f65-93D0-3DB3A80A0BE0} We need a standardized mechanical building block that aligns with the dominant power ranges while minimizing unique cabinet variants. Modularity - Sales eaGUID: {CFCFDD33-AB36-4273-B53B-B3DB8B2E5827} 4B hits the sweet spot of the core MHE market, including 10 kW lithium applications. files.contentPreview: Stackable, Connectable Architecture The cabinet architecture shall support physical stacking and mechanical connection of enclosures to extend power output beyond a single cabinet-s capacity. In addition, the architecture shall support configurations where a stacked system can charge 2 vehicles concurrently (dual-output operation). Engineering Question - Single Drop eaGUID: {F36E2CCD-5066-40fc-A889-3AA850FF2698} If the dual controller option selected, is this from a single drop from the grid? Each additional enclosure introduces incremental system cost (filters, power supply, interface board, labor). files.contentPreview: EN 1175 4.3.6 Protection from residual voltages 4.3.6 Protection from residual voltages After disconnecting energy sources, the voltage of the capacitors in power circuits shall be less than 60 V DC after 10 s. If the above condition is not technically achievable or practicable a warning/safety label shall be provided. This warning label shall be permanent and indelible and shall be affixed on, or in close proximity to, the enclosure containing the capacitors. NOTE Safety signs EN ISO 7010 W001 and EN ISO 7010 W012 can be used.

files.relativePath: Model/IPC !/03 Product Requirement/Regulatory Requirements/EN/EN 1175/EN 1175 2020/EN 1175 Annex D (normative) Electric drive system (motors, converters, generators, energy sources)/EN 1175 D.2 Special requirements/EN 1175 D.2.4 Type plates.md
files.contentPreview: EN 1175 D.2.4 Type plates D.2.4 Type plates The components of electric drive systems shall be provided with indelible and not easily detachable type plates. Type plates of motors and converters shall include information ensuring traceability e.g. a serial number. To inhibit unexpected or uncontrollable movements of the electric drive system the terminal marking shall ensure for example the right connection of the wiring with the components or the correct exchange with spare parts. Terminal marking shall be in accordance with EN 60034-8. Components of the electric drive system with nominal voltages of the energy source greater than 96 V or equipped with a high-power energy source (e.g. electric double layer capacitors) shall be marked with a durable hazard or warning labels.

files.contentPreview: IEC 62752 6.1.0-1 The IC-CPD shall be marked in a durable manner with the following data: a) the manufacturer's or distributor’s name or trademark; b) type designation, catalogue number or serial number; c) rated voltage; d) rated frequency, if the IC-CPD is designed for frequencies other than 50 Hz and 60 Hz (see 5.3.6); e) rated current; f) rated residual operating current; g) degree of protection. The IP degree is applicable only to the function box and marking g) shall be on the function box; h) the marking with the name of the product: IC-CPD; j) IC-CPD shall be marked with the symbol -25 ; k) for IC-CPD according to 4.5.2, a statement that the IC-CPD may not operate if used on IT or other unearthed systems such as an isolated winding generator or isolating transformer. files.contentPreview: IEC 62752 8.3.11.2.0-1 IC-CPDs shall be provided with a flexible copper cable complying with IEC 60227 or IEC 60245. NOTE IEC 62893 for EV charging cables is under development. The minimum cross-sectional areas of the load conductors and the protective earth conductor are given in Table 6 in relation to the current limit given by the control pilot signal. The control pilot wire shall have a minimum cross-section of 0,5 mm²/AWG20. Compliance is checked by inspection, by measurement and by checking that the flexible cables or cords are in accordance with the IEC 60227 series or the IEC 60245 series, as applicable.

files.contentPreview: IEC 62752 8.5.1.0-1 IC-CPDs shall be so designed that, when they are used according to the manufacturers' instructions, live parts are not accessible. External parts, other than screws or other means for fixing covers and labels, which are accessible when the IC-CPD is used under normal conditions, shall either be of insulating material, or be lined throughout with insulating material, unless the live parts are within an internal enclosure of insulating material. Such lining shall be fixed so that it is not likely to be lost. It shall have adequate thickness and mechanical strength and shall provide adequate protection even at places where sharp edges occur. Inlet openings for cables shall either be of insulating material or be provided with bushing or similar devices of insulating material. files.contentPreview: IEC 62752 9.7.9.0-1 The IC-CPD shall be installed as for normal use. The device under test is supplied by a power source, according to Figure 28, and is powered at 1,1 times the rated voltage. The following test procedure is applied. a) The switch S2 being in closed position, the switch S1 is closed. The contacts of the IC-CPD shall close. b) The switched S2 being in opened position, the switch S1 is closed. The contacts of the IC-CPD shall not close. c) The switch S1 and S2 being in the closed position, the contacts of the IC-CPD shall be closed. If the switch S2 is suddenly opened, the contacts of the IC-CPD shall open in less than 0,1 s. After closing of S1, some time may elapse before closing of the IC-CPD. Afterwards, the test is repeated but with the device being supplied at 0,85 Ue.

files.contentPreview: SAE ARP1816E 3.1.5.2.1 A grounded electrostatic or Faraday shield shall be placed between the primary and secondary windings. This shield shall be made of copper or aluminum and shall have at least the ampacity of the primary conductor if the primary conductor is smaller than No. 6 AWG (16 mm2). If the primary conductor is No. 6 AWG (16 mm2) or larger, the shield shall have an ampacity of at least 50% of the primary conductor. If foil is used it shall have a thickness of not less than 0.25 mm (0.010 inch).

files.contentPreview: UL 2237 10.7 The tightening torque for a field-wiring terminal shall be specified by the device manufacturer and the device shall be marked in accordance with 48.7. The tightening torque shall not be less than 90% of the value required for the Static Heating Test in the Standard for Equipment Wiring Terminals for Use with Aluminum and/or Copper Conductors, UL 486E, for the maximum wire size corresponding to the ampere rating of the device. Exception: A lesser torque value meets the intent of the requirement if the connector complies with the Standard for Wire Connectors, UL 486A-486B, or the Standard for Equipment Wiring Terminals for Use with Aluminum and/or Copper Conductors, UL 486E, using the lesser torque value.

files.contentPreview: UL 1012 7.1.10 7.1.10 With regard to 7.1.7, if openings in the enclosure are provided, it will also necessitate the use of a barrier: a) Under wire, unless it is of the flame-retardant type, such as neoprene- or thermoplastic- insulated wire; and b) Under a fuse, unless a complete, unventilated enclosure is provided for each fuse. Exception: A barrier is not needed under: a) A supplementary fuse; b) A fuse connected in a Class 2 circuit; c) An individually enclosed fuse such as an extractor fuse; or d) A fuse within a complete unventilated enclosure. Consideration will be given to a fuse enclosed within a transformer winding.
